chapters.title: Chapter 102: Spoils of Survival [2]
paragraphs: Since Soren and Ryan had been carted off to the hospital unconscious, the Bureau workers had to step in to retrieve the rest of the cores and loot from the scene, taking a standard processing fee before handling the payout.

’Although we lost some money due to that, it’s definitely better than losing everything,’ Soren reasoned, finding the silver lining. Then, as if recalling something, his eyes narrowed into a slight squint.
’We still have to discuss how to handle the monolith...’
According to Sister Zoe, the Bureau had also managed to dig up and transport the massive structure out of the gate during their cleanup operation. However, she didn’t know more than that.

According to the law, any unique artifacts or anomalies unearthed within a gate technically belonged to the awakeners who cleared it, provided they registered the discovery. However, when it came to something as unprecedented and potentially hazardous as a monolith, the state always reserved the right to step in under national security protocols.

However, Soren knew exactly what kind of terrifying potential was packed into that stone structure. That’s exactly why he hoped the Bureau wouldn’t try to use those protocols to permanently confiscate it.

At the same time, he couldn’t help but wonder if their research teams could even discover what it actually did. Without the right appraisal methods, they might just see it as a highly volatile, dangerous battery and completely miss its true function.
’They’ll probably contact us once their initial analysis is complete,’ he mused.
For now, speculating was useless. He needed to ensure that when that meeting finally happened, he had enough personal leverage and strength to avoid being pushed around by the authorities.
If possible, he wanted to keep it for himself, so he planned to do his best to negotiate or fight for his rights when the time came.
Shifting his thoughts back to the present, Soren took a deep breath and let the future worries fade away.
He let his eyes land on the last remaining object on the training mattress: the manual.

It was the technique hidden within the Ring of Boundless Void, a personal gift from the Sunless Emperor. He had been stopping himself from looking at it until now, deliberately holding back his curiosity until he had enough privacy.
’Let’s see what kind of treasure this is~’

With a flicker of excitement, Soren reached out and picked up the manual. The moment his fingers brushed the cover, a strange, profound sensation washed over his skin, like holding a cold piece of the night sky itself.
His anticipation growing, he gripped the edge of the cover and opened it.
’...Why isn’t it opening?’

Soren frowned. He increased his strength, pulling at the pages with enough force to tear ordinary parchment, but the book remained completely unyielding, its pages sealed shut like a solid block of steel. He was completely dumbfounded.

Refusing to give up, he channeled a thin strand of mana through his fingertips, infusing it directly into the cover. When that didn’t provoke a single reaction, he bit the tip of his thumb and let a drop of blood fall onto the binding, testing the classic recognition methods.
Still, nothing happened. The manual sat in his hands, completely inert and stubbornly closed.

Staring at the uselessly sealed book, Soren let out a dry laugh. Then, a sudden realization hit him. Recalling that he possessed a literal cheat ability designed for evaluating hidden value, he focused his gaze and quickly used Investor’s Insight on it.
A crisp chime echoed in his mind as the familiar translucent interface flickered to life over the ancient cover.
[Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra]
Classification: Mental Cultivation Method / Spiritual Intent Refinement
Rank: Legendary
Current Status: Restricted / Sealed (Gender Mismatch Detected)
Requirements to Unseal: Female Gender, Innate Mana Sensitivity, Calmed Mindscape.

[Description]: A high-tier heritage technique originating from an ancient lineage of cosmic cultivators. It utilizes the naturally delicate, flexible, and intricate spiritual pathways unique to female consciousness to map the mind according to the alignment of the stars.
[Core Effects]:

- Stellar Filament Construction: Transforms raw mental energy into microscopic, luminous threads of starlight. These filaments can extend outside the body, remaining entirely invisible and untraceable to ordinary senses and standard detection spells.
- Constellation Mapping: Allows the practitioner to weave these mental threads into complex sensory arrays or direct offensive webs.

[True Potential]: At mastery, the user can use these invisible threads for flawless, long-range telekinetic manipulation, track targets across vast distances, or directly invade an enemy’s mindscape to sever their thoughts, effectively paralyzing their cognitive functions.
Soren stared at the description, his jaw dropping slightly as he read through the details.
A Legendary rank technique.
Even in his wildest guesses, he hadn’t expected the Sunless Emperor to drop something this monumental.
Then, his eyes drifted back up to the requirement section, and the corner of his eye twitched.
’Gender Mismatch Detected...’
A helpless, dry chuckle escaped his lips as he shook his head, looking down at the stubbornly sealed book.

He had been racking his brain trying to figure out why a legendary entity would hand him a useless brick, but as his eyes lingered on the strict activation requirements, the pieces began to fall into place.

The Sunless Emperor hadn’t chosen this manual at random; he had specifically selected a solution tailored for his wife, Ethea, after listening to Soren describe her paralyzed condition during their encounter. That ancient powerhouse had actually taken those details to heart, intentionally passing down a legacy that bypassed physical limitations entirely.
And given Ethea’s quiet nature and the immense mental focus she probably possessed, a technique that relied on a calm, intricate mindscape was an absolute, flawless match for her.
As he focused on the specific effects listed on the screen, the gift’s true utility became clear.
’Invisible spiritual threads, telekinesis, and cognitive paralysis...’
His initial annoyance entirely evaporated into a deep sense of satisfaction.
If she could master this, her physical confinement would no longer completely isolate her from the world.
With invisible threads and telekinesis, she would be able to interact with her surroundings, lift objects, and essentially ’move’ things through her sheer willpower.
It was a beautiful alternative to her immobility, granting her a profound level of freedom and independence that her own body denied her.

chapters.title: Chapter 103: Gift [1]
paragraphs: ’With this, she won’t feel as helpless as before.’
Feeling a massive weight lift off his chest, Soren gently ran his hand over the sealed cover one last time before carefully placing the manual back into the Ring of Boundless Void, keeping it safe.
But as the translucent screen faded from his vision, a sudden wave of practical questions flooded his mind.
How did one actually learn and cultivate a technique like this? Did it require standard mana to activate, or did it rely entirely on the user’s raw mental energy?
If mana was required, could Ethea even cultivate it at all?

She was paralyzed, meaning her physical pathways were blocked, but her mindscape should have remained intact or less affected. If the sutra truly bypassed the physical form as the description implied, her condition shouldn’t be an issue, but the uncertainty still lingered.
And then there was the most immediate problem.
How should he even give it to her?
He couldn’t exactly tell her that a peerless entity from another distant realm had hand-delivered a legendary technique specifically for her. He needed a believable story.
’Should I just say I found it inside the Golden Gate?’ Soren pondered inwardly.
The more he thought about it, the more it made perfect sense.

It was both true and entirely plausible. The Golden Gate was an unprecedented anomaly filled with unknown treasures, making it the perfect cover. He had no other reasonable excuse that wouldn’t sound like complete madness.

Although she would still be suspicious of how a legendary manual tailored so perfectly for her condition just happened to drop from a random gate, even if it was a Golden one, she wouldn’t push him for answers she knew he couldn’t give.
They had that unspoken understanding between them now.
With his cover story decided, Soren quickly cleared the remaining items from the mattress and sat down in a comfortable lotus position.
Reaching into his storage ring, he pulled out a few high-grade mana crystals.
’...Hm. Time to cultivate.’

If possible, he wanted to reach the peak of the 2nd circle or even break through before he was ready to dive into the gates again. The incident was a reminder that his current strength was simply not enough to guarantee his own safety, let alone others.
Placing the crystals in his lap, he closed his eyes and began to circulate his core. He drew in a deep breath, focusing his mind on the raw, unrefined energy locked within the stones.
Slowly, thin wisps of brilliant mana began to drift from the crystals, sinking directly into his skin and flowing along his pathways.
Gradually, the external world dissolved into absolute stillness as the rhythmic flow of energy pulled him under, plunging him into a timeless trance.

Soren finally opened his eyes, took a slow breath, shook off the residual numbness in his limbs, and felt the small but noticeable difference in his body. His mana pathways were pulsing with a slightly denser, more refined flow of energy, showing clear progress toward the peak of the second circle.
A quick glance at his device revealed that hours had flown by, and it was already late in the evening.
After washing away the thin layer of impurities expelled during his cultivation, he walked out of the training room and joined Ethea and Aunt Clara for dinner.
Once they finished eating, Aunt Clara helped Ethea navigate her evening routine, taking care of her bathroom needs and helping her freshen up for the night.
With Ethea comfortably settled, Aunt Clara began finishing up the last of her chores around the kitchen, preparing to take her leave for the night.
Before she could pack up her things, Soren gestured toward the dining table. "Aunt Clara, could you sit down with us for a moment before you head out? There are a few things I’d like to discuss."
Clara looked slightly surprised but nodded warmly, pulling out a chair across from them.

"First of all, I just sent a transfer to your account," Soren said, tapping his screen to finalize the transaction. "It’s a bonus for staying by Ethea’s side at the hospital all day while I was unconscious. I deeply appreciate the extra care and effort you put in.
Aunt Clara checked her device, her eyes widening as she read the notification. "Mr. Soren, this is far too much for just..."

"You earned every bit of it, so please just accept it," Soren countered smoothly, cutting off her polite refusal before transitioning to the main topic. "More importantly, I want to discuss making this a permanent arrangement. I’d like to offer you full employment with a fixed, full-time schedule."
He pulled up a digital contract draft on his screen, presenting a monthly credit salary that sat significantly higher than the standard market rate for caretaking.

"I want to ensure you are well compensated for your time," Soren added, keeping his tone earnest. "Having someone reliable here consistently gives me the freedom to focus better on my work without constantly worrying about the household."

"The salary is far more than enough," Aunt Clara said, her expression softening as she glanced over at Ethea. "But truly, I would have stayed regardless. I’ve grown incredibly fond of Miss Ethea this past month, and she has been an absolute joy to care for. If you will have me, I would be more than happy to make this permanent."
Hearing her words, Ethea looked up and offered a warm smile. "Thank you, Aunt Clara."
Soren nodded in deep appreciation, matching her sentiment. "Thank you. We really appreciate everything you do for us."
With the core decision settled, they agreed to finalize the formal contract details tomorrow.
Aunt Clara then bid them both a warm goodnight before finally taking her leave.
Once the door clicked shut behind her, the apartment fell into a deep stillness.
Soren walked over and switched on the television to provide some background noise.
Sitting down beside Ethea, he took a quiet glance at her profile as the changing colors of the screen reflected in her eyes.
"Ethea, there’s something I want to give you..."

chapters.title: Chapter 104: Gift [2]
paragraphs: Ethea paused, turning her head toward him. Her expression remained neutral, but Soren had learned to read her well enough to know it was her way of listening.
He reached into his inventory and pulled out the manual, holding it out for her to see.
Noticing the confusion in her eyes, Soren explained, "I found this inside the Golden Gate. However, it can only be learned by females."
Ethea’s interest was clearly piqued, but she looked from the book back up to his face, her tone changing slightly. "...Why are you giving it to me? Do you... want me to check what it is?"
"Huh?" Soren was caught off guard by her question, but he quickly found his footing. "No, no," he replied, shaking his head. "I was going to give it to you regardless. Because..."
"Well, anyway, let’s just open it, and you’ll understand everything soon."
Although a flicker of suspicion crossed her features, Ethea silently acquiesced.

Soren leaned forward and carefully placed the manual onto her lap. He then gently covered her hands with his own, carefully guiding them toward the sealed cover to help her lift it. Ethea was visibly startled by the sudden physical contact, her shoulders stiffening slightly, but she didn’t pull back. She remained silent, allowing him to move her hands into place.
The moment their joined fingers brushed the surface, the manual reacted.

The heavy cover began to move, slowly lifting open on its own as if answering an invisible command. But just as it unsealed halfway, the texture of the solid parchment seemed to fracture, bleeding into a liquid brilliance that slipped right through their fingers. The solid book simply ceased to exist, melting away into a swirl of dazzling, mysterious lights that left no heat behind. Before Soren could even process what was happening, the light shot directly toward Ethea’s forehead.
"Ethea!"
Soren’s eyes widened in sheer panic.
He instinctively reached out, but it was already too late.
The light sank completely into her brow, and her eyes were already closed, her head slumping back as if she had suddenly fallen into a deep sleep.
He immediately pressed his fingers against her neck, breathing a small sigh of relief when he felt the steady, calm rhythm of her pulse.
Hoping to get a clearer picture of what was happening to her, he fixed his gaze on her and silently activated Investor’s Insight, then focused on the two most important lines.
[Status: Unconscious]
[Mental State: Mindscape Enlightening (Trance)]
"Hmm."

Soren squinted at the blue interface, a familiar memory flashing through his mind. Was she experiencing the same thing he had? It looked exactly like the process of receiving an inheritance, just like the one he had gone through back then.
Still, the uncertainty kept his muscles tense.
He couldn’t just sit around and do nothing.

Reaching back into his storage ring, he pulled out a few high-grade recovery potions and lined them up on the table within arm’s reach. He kept his eyes locked on her face, watching for any sign of discomfort or sudden change, ready to act the second anything went wrong.
’Please be safe,’ He thought, his fist clenching as he stared at her peaceful expression. ’Please... just wake up okay.’
Ethea opened her eyes.
’Where am I?’

She looked around, the words remaining an unspoken thought in the vast emptiness. The familiar walls of the apartment and the dull hum of the television had vanished. Instead, she was surrounded by a boundless, silent void of deep indigo, stretching infinitely in every direction.
But the true shock came from below.
She... She was standing.
For the first time in what felt like an eternity, she could feel the solid pressure of a floor beneath her soles, even though there wasn’t any.
Curving her fingers, she watched them move exactly as she intended.
’...Gulp.’
She tilted her head, shifted her weight, shook her arms and waist, and took a tentative step forward.
The crushing weight that usually anchored her physical body to the wheelchair was entirely gone.
’I can move?’
A sudden rush of warmth flooded her chest, a mixture of disbelief and a raw, long-forgotten thrill.

She raised her hands to her face, staring at her palms as she squeezed them into tight fists, then released them. She could feel every joint, every muscle responding instantly to her thoughts. It felt so incredibly light.
Before she could lose herself in the sheer joy of movement, the deep indigo void around her began to ripple.

A single droplet of silver light welled up from the void beneath her feet, floating upward past her chest. Then another followed, and another, until thousands of glowing silver particles began to rise around her like upside-down rain.
The lights coalesced, flattening and sharpening into elegant, complex characters that formed a massive, circular wall of ancient script.
She had never seen these symbols before, yet the moment her eyes brushed against them, their meaning echoed directly within her consciousness.
’...Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra.’
As the name resonated in her mind, the wall of text began to constrict, slowly rotating around her in a tightening spiral.
One by one, the glowing characters began to drift toward her, sinking directly into her mind without a sound.

With every word that dissolved into her, a vast flood of instinctual knowledge unlocked. She could feel the technique anchoring itself directly to her consciousness, rewriting her understanding of how to exert power.
As the realization settled, the entire void responded to the shift within her.
The revolving sea of script accelerated into a bright vortex, obscuring everything else and immersing her entirely in the technique.
Time lost all meaning inside the vast emptiness as the remnants of the vortex were completely absorbed into her being.
Gradually, the boundless void receded, drawing her awareness back.
Ethea opened her eyes, a brilliant silver light flashing through her pupils. For a brief moment, her eyes filled with a dense cluster of tiny, rotating stars before returning to their usual color.

An underlying aura of quiet power now wrapped around her, reshaping her entire demeanor with a newfound, profound stillness. The immediate space surrounding her held a faint, shimmering haze where tiny specks of starlight drifted like dust motes, visible to anyone looking closely.

With her consciousness fully returned, she felt the heavy anchor of her physical body once more. Along with that physical awareness came a pure, warm presence sitting right beside her, holding her hands firmly and gently within their own.
Feeling the slight tremble of his worried touch, the corners of her lips curved upward into a soft, beautiful smile.
’Soren... I’m so glad you’re by my side.’

She looked around, the words remaining an unspoken thought in the vast emptiness.
The familiar walls of the apartment and the dull hum of the television had vanished.
Instead, she was surrounded by a boundless, silent void of deep indigo, stretching infinitely in every direction.
But the true shock came from below.
She...
She was standing.
For the first time in what felt like an eternity, she could feel the solid pressure of a floor beneath her soles, even though there wasn’t any.
Curving her fingers, she watched them move exactly as she intended.
’...Gulp.’
She tilted her head, shifted her weight, shook her arms and waist, and took a tentative step forward.
The crushing weight that usually anchored her physical body to the wheelchair was entirely gone.
’I can move?’
A sudden rush of warmth flooded her chest, a mixture of disbelief and a raw, long-forgotten thrill.
She raised her hands to her face, staring at her palms as she squeezed them into tight fists, then released them.
She could feel every joint, every muscle responding instantly to her thoughts.
It felt so incredibly light.
Before she could lose herself in the sheer joy of movement, the deep indigo void around her began to ripple.
A single droplet of silver light welled up from the void beneath her feet, floating upward past her chest.
Then another followed, and another, until thousands of glowing silver particles began to rise around her like upside-down rain.
The lights coalesced, flattening and sharpening into elegant, complex characters that formed a massive, circular wall of ancient script.
She had never seen these symbols before, yet the moment her eyes brushed against them, their meaning echoed directly within her consciousness.
’...Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra.’
As the name resonated in her mind, the wall of text began to constrict, slowly rotating around her in a tightening spiral.
One by one, the glowing characters began to drift toward her, sinking directly into her mind without a sound.
With every word that dissolved into her, a vast flood of instinctual knowledge unlocked.
She could feel the technique anchoring itself directly to her consciousness, rewriting her understanding of how to exert power.
As the realization settled, the entire void responded to the shift within her.
The revolving sea of script accelerated into a bright vortex, obscuring everything else and immersing her entirely in the technique.
Time lost all meaning inside the vast emptiness as the remnants of the vortex were completely absorbed into her being.
Gradually, the boundless void receded, drawing her awareness back.
Ethea opened her eyes, a brilliant silver light flashing through her pupils.
For a brief moment, her eyes filled with a dense cluster of tiny, rotating stars before returning to their usual color.
An underlying aura of quiet power now wrapped around her, reshaping her entire demeanor with a newfound, profound stillness.
The immediate space surrounding her held a faint, shimmering haze where tiny specks of starlight drifted like dust motes, visible to anyone looking closely.
With her consciousness fully returned, she felt the heavy anchor of her physical body once more.
Along with that physical awareness came a pure, warm presence sitting right beside her, holding her hands firmly and gently within their own.
Feeling the slight tremble of his worried touch, the corners of her lips curved upward into a soft, beautiful smile.
’Soren...
I’m so glad you’re by my side.’

chapters.title: Chapter 105: Melting Hearts
paragraphs: Soren kept his eyes locked on Ethea, his gaze shifting back and forth between her peaceful face and the blue interface floating in front of him.
About ten minutes ticked by in heavy silence, the quiet room stretching the seconds. He barely blinked, watching for the slightest change in her breathing or any twitch of discomfort.
Finally, a subtle shift caught his attention.
The lines on the status window flickered, the words updating as the trance state shifted back to normal. At that exact moment, her long eyelashes imperceptibly fluttered.
Ethea opened her eyes, and their gazes met.

Soren found himself lost in her eyes for a brief, breathless moment, completely captivated by the faint, residual starlight swirling deep within her pupils before he managed to pull himself back to reality.
He cleared his throat and asked. "Ethea? How do you feel?"
"...I am okay."

As she spoke, her gaze drifted downward, focusing on where their fingers were still intertwined. Following her eyes, Soren suddenly realized his own actions. He had been tightly gripping her hands the entire time without even noticing. He quickly let go, pulling his arms back as the sharp tension that had locked his shoulders finally evaporated.

He waited a moment for her to adjust, though the burning curiosity inside him could no longer be contained. Leaning forward slightly, curiosity and a spark of hope mixing in his tone, he asked, "What happened? Did you... learn it?"
"Mm," Ethea nodded slightly. "The technique is integrated into my mind. I can practice it now. And..."
She paused, looking down at her empty hands where his warmth still lingered before settling them on her lap.
"Soren, I..."
She clenched her fingers, gathering her courage, and raised her head, locking her eyes directly with his, refusing to look away.
Thump.
The quiet room suddenly felt much smaller.
"I am truly grateful.
"I am grateful for everything. For this gift, for the sweets you always bring me, and for the meals you carefully prepare."

Soren was frozen, caught completely off guard by her sudden openness. He found himself entirely unable to look away from her. The usual emotional wall she kept between them felt entirely gone, replaced by a raw, quiet sincerity.

"Thank you for always thinking of me too," she added, her voice dropping to a softer, more intimate register. "For taking care of me, worrying about me, and always trying to help me, even when I do not ask."

A faint, genuine warmth flushed her cheeks, making her look incredibly lovely in the quiet room. She squeezed her hands together in her lap, her heart fluttering at her own boldness, yet she forced herself to keep looking at him.
Thump. Thump.
"Thank you..."
"Thank you for being such a good husband to me, Soren."
Soren felt his breath catch completely in his throat.
Thump. Thump.
Before he could even process the sweet, racing beat of his own heart, Ethea took a small, steadying breath. Her expression remained gentle, but a beautiful, unwavering determination filled her eyes.
"I promise to fulfill my role as your wife as well. I will master this technique so that I won’t be a burden to you."

The room fell back into absolute stillness, save for the wild, loud ringing in Soren’s ears. He sat there, utterly paralyzed, his chest tight as he stared at the girl in front of him. Her cheeks were still tinged with a soft pink, and though she looked completely calm on the outside, the slight tremor in her clasped fingers betrayed how much courage those words had taken.
"Ethea..."
Soren finally managed to squeeze out, his voice a bit rougher than usual.
He reached out, his hand hovering in the air for a second before he gently placed it over hers once more. This time, his touch was slow and deliberate.
"You have never been a burden," he said, his eyes filled with an intense, quiet sincerity that mirrored her own. "Not even for a single second."
Ethea’s eyes widened once more.

The absolute certainty in his voice left no room for doubt, and the soft pink hue rapidly deepened across her cheeks. She quietly shifted her gaze away, her usual detached composure melting into a rare, defenseless vulnerability.
Only then, as the initial urgency of comforting her faded, did the delayed realization of her words finally crash through his brain.
’Wait... What did she just say?’
’...Good husband?’
His mind completely short-circuited.

In the silence that followed, he found himself staring at her, noticing the delicate curve of her shoulders and the gentle, flushed expression that made her look so entirely different from her usual self. Her quiet shyness made her look absolutely adorable, a pure and lovely sight that made it impossible for him to tear his eyes away.
"...Gulp."
The sound of his own nervous swallow seemed to break the spell, and immediately after, a sudden, fierce heat rushed straight to his ears.
Thump. Thump.
Spurred by the erratic rhythm in his chest, Soren frantically pulled his hand back as if he had been burned, quickly turning his face toward the wall.
He coughed into his fist, trying to swallow down the sudden nervousness fluttering in his chest, but his heart refused to listen, hammering wildly against his ribs.

"I—I mean," he stammered, his fingers blindly scratching the back of his neck as he scrambled to piece his composure back together. "You really do not have to say things like that. We are... we are married, after all. It is only natural that I take care of the meals, the sweets, and... and you..."
He kept his eyes glued to the far corner of the room, his red ears completely betraying the calm front he was trying to put on.
Desperate to escape the sweet, suffocating tension that seemed to shrink the entire apartment, he cleared his throat loudly and grabbed the nearest conversational lifeline.
"Cough! Anyway! The manual... it is great that you learned it. Really great. What kind of technique is it? Is it safe to practice?"

chapters.title: Chapter 106: The Novice No. 2
paragraphs: "You have never been a burden. Not even for a single second."
Ethea’s beating heart suddenly intensified, hammering wildly against her ribs. She quickly turned away in shame, unable to face him any longer.
’Why did I say all of that?’
’Urgh, so embarrassing.’

A deep flush crept up her face. She felt completely exposed, her mind racing with regret over her own sudden boldness. Sure, she was going to express her gratitude, but not that much! And certainly not confessing her intentions!
’What is he going to think of me now?’
The agonizing worry began to chew at her composure, making the quiet room feel entirely too small.
With each passing second, the lack of any response from him grew heavier until she simply could no longer bear the tense silence.
She secretly took a peek at Soren, bracing herself to find him looking as clueless as ever.
However, the sight that met her eyes made her freeze in absolute shock.

Soren was staring directly at her, looking as though his brain had entirely ceased to function. His usual composed expression was shattered; a distinct flush covered his cheeks, and the tips of his ears were slightly red.

As she watched him, she saw him take a sharp, heavy gulp, his eyes widening in sudden panic. Then, he abruptly moved away, violently pulling his hand back and turning his face completely toward the wall.
Ethea fell completely silent, a sudden sense of déjà vu washing over her as she stared at the side of his head.
’...Is he... embarrassed too?’

Watching him act so utterly flustered, the lingering anxiety in her chest instantly vanished, replaced by an absolute certainty. He was completely panicked. In fact, looking at the furious red color expanding across his ears, he was reacting just like her, or even worse than her. A small wave of relief began to settle over her, seeing that she wasn’t the only one losing her mind.
However, the moment he started stammering out his excuse about meals and sweets, her newfound calm vanished.
"We are... we are married, after all. It is only natural that I take care of the meals, the sweets, and..."
"...and you..."
At his last word, ’you’, Ethea’s heart skipped a beat.
Her face flared with a fresh, burning blush.
’Urgh!’

She silently cursed him in her mind for saying something so devastatingly direct, even when he was clearly drowning in his own awkwardness. But deep down, a warm, sweet feeling bloomed inside her chest, completely melting away the last remnants of her shame.
"Cough..."
As Soren loudly cleared his throat and frantically started rambling about the manual, desperately trying to shift the topic, Ethea’s lips unconsciously curled upward into a soft smile.
Watching him stubbornly keep his eyes glued to the far corner of the room while ’admiring’ the blank wall, a single word naturally drifted through her thoughts.
’Cute~’
She let her gaze linger on his profile for a moment longer before his frantic rambling eventually ground to a halt, leaving the room in a sudden, heavy silence.
Ethea kept her lips sealed, deliberately choosing to let the quiet stretch as she thoroughly savored the rare sight of his complete lack of composure.
Watching him struggle to find his footing like a boy caught misbehaving, a soft wave of amusement washed over her.
’It seems like I’m not the only novice here. Hehe~’
Besides, the sheer contrast between his usual calm and this current, flustered mess was just too entertaining to rush.

On the other hand, misinterpreting her silence, a flash of genuine anxiety suddenly broke through Soren’s embarrassment. The frantic heat on his face instantly gave way to concern, and he snapped his head back around to look at her, his brow furrowed.
"Ethea?" he called out, his voice sharp with worry. "Is something wrong? Does it hurt somewhere?"

Watching him completely abandon his own embarrassment the moment he thought she might be in danger sent a fresh wave of warmth straight to her chest. A quiet sense of joy bloomed within her, making her secretly happy that his immediate instinct was to prioritize her safety above everything else.
Gently smoothing out the fabric of her skirt, she offered a soft, reassuring nod to ease his sudden panic.
"It is entirely safe," she replied quietly, her voice carrying a steady rhythm that instantly calmed the room’s frantic energy. "There is no pain or discomfort. You do not need to worry."

Soren let out a sigh of relief. Then, acting as if his chaotic meltdown from just a moment ago had never even happened, he quickly moved over to the nearby sofa and sat down, completely eager to bury the awkwardness under a wave of normal conversation.
"That’s good," he said, clearing his throat once more to stabilize his voice. "So, how exactly does it work? You can practice it, right?"

Ethea watched him settle into the cushions, easily seeing straight through his clumsy attempt at pretending. It was entirely obvious that he was just trying to sweep his embarrassment under the rug, but she chose not to expose him, letting him have his escape lifeline. Well, it was good for her as well.

"It is difficult to explain with just words, because the technique operates entirely on the mind and the spirit. But with it... I might even be able to move my body. I will show you the results myself once I master it to a certain extent."

Hearing her words, a warm smile finally broke through Soren’s lingering awkwardness. As long as the method was truly useful and brought her closer to recovering her mobility, that was more than enough for him.
"I’ll hold you to that promise then," Soren said, his tone turning lighter and encouraging. "Take all the time you need to practice. There’s absolutely no rush."

Seeing his smile, Ethea felt a sudden wave of disappointment wash over her. She secretly wished he would stay flustered or show a bit more of that adorable, nervous side from earlier, rather than switching back to his usual supportive, stable self so quickly.
However, her disappointment quickly shifted into a different kind of regret.
"I wish I could share this method with you," she murmured, her voice laced with genuine sadness. "If it were possible for you to learn it as well, you would become much stronger. And..."
’I wouldn’t have to worry about you so much, either.’

chapters.title: Chapter 107: Uncharted Paths
paragraphs: "Don’t worry about that," Soren chuckled softly, completely untroubled by her words. "As long as you can learn it and benefit from it, that’s completely fine with me. Besides, the technique is exclusively for females anyway. I couldn’t use it even if I wanted to."
Ethea fell silent for a brief moment, her eyes fixed on his calm, reassuring face. A fierce, quiet determination took root deep within her chest as she made a silent vow.
’Then I will just have to develop one for you myself.’
With that silent promise echoing in her mind, a comfortable, lingering warmth finally replaced the chaotic tension in the room.
Across from her, Soren took a sip of tea, his posture fully returning to its usual steady, dependable state, completely unaware of the monumental task his wife had just set for herself.

Modifying or creating a technique from scratch was a feat usually reserved for Emperors or even stronger figures who possessed immense experience. For someone in her current, crippled state to even attempt it with a legendary-grade heritage technique like the Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra was pure madness.
Yet, Ethea didn’t feel a single shred of doubt.
Well, it’s not like she hasn’t done it before.

With that grounding realization, she let the ambitious thought drift to the back of her mind and relaxed back into her seat as Soren switched the display screen back on to finish the broadcast. They quietly watched the rest of the program together before he carefully carried her back to the bedroom, bringing a peaceful end to a night that had changed everything between them.
Over the next few days, Soren remained at home, splitting his time between his own training and accompanying Ethea.
The constant proximity naturally shrank the distance between them, melting away the old formal barriers until their daily interactions felt completely effortless.
Yet, a strange new friction quietly took its place.

Whenever he lifted her from her seat or leaned in close to adjust her blankets, his movements would suddenly stall, his hands hovering for a fraction of a second as if he had suddenly forgotten how to breathe.
He found himself tracking the subtle curve of her lips when she smiled, only to abruptly snap his gaze away and clear his throat the moment she caught him looking.

He couldn’t understand why a simple, accidental brush of their fingers now sent a sudden jolt straight to his chest, but the inexplicable awkwardness left him meticulously policing his every move, desperately trying to look normal while hyper-aware of her every breath.
Fortunately, he was finally heading out today.
After his morning appointment, he intended to take some time for himself to clear his head and figure out why his own body was suddenly acting like a broken script around her.
"I’ll be back by dinner, stay safe," Soren said, offering a brief wave to Ethea and Clara before stepping through the front door.

Twenty minutes later, the taxi pulled up outside a modest apartment building situated just a short distance from the city center. Soren stepped out into the crisp air and lightly stretched his arms, hearing a satisfying pop in his shoulders.
’Perhaps I should just buy a car soon,’ he mused, noting how much time he was spending on commutes lately.

Pulling his phone from his pocket, he glanced at the screen to double-check the address one last time. Confirming he was at the right place, he slipped the device away, entered the building, and took the stairs. He maintained a steady pace until he reached the fifth floor, stopping directly in front of the door number listed in his messages, and firmly pressed the doorbell.
A moment later, the door clicked open, and a familiar, youthful face popped out.
"Oh, you’re here, sir!"
"Mmm." Soren offered a nod. " And I told you, you can just call me Brother Soren, Ryan."
The boy gave an embarrassed nod and quickly stepped aside, gesturing for him to come in. "Please come inside, we have been waiting for you."
"Excuse me," Soren murmured, stepping over the threshold.

Ryan led him down the short hallway and into the cozy living room, where the rest of his family was gathered. The moment his sibling and parents noticed his arrival, they immediately stood up from the sofa, their posture straight with a mix of deep respect and nervous anticipation.
They exchanged greetings quickly.
"Please, come in! It is an honor to have you in our home," Ryan’s father said, stepping forward with an open, welcoming smile to shake Soren’s hand warmly.
"Thank you for having me," Soren replied, returning the firm handshake before exchanging polite greetings with Ryan’s mother and younger sister.
The family eagerly gestured for him to take the most comfortable seat in the living room.

Once everyone had settled down, Ryan’s mother quickly disappeared into the kitchen, returning a moment later with a large, steaming platter of freshly made dumplings. The savory aroma instantly filled the cozy space.
"You must be hungry after your trip here. Please, eat up while they are still hot," she urged, placing a fork and a small side dish in front of him.
Soren didn’t stand on ceremony at the sight of one of his favorite meals.
’I guess this is why he asked me about it.’
He chuckled inwardly before taking a bite of a dumpling, the rich, flavorful filling hitting the spot perfectly.
"These are excellent, thank you," he said, genuinely enjoying the meal.

For the next ten or more minutes, they exchanged relaxed small talk, discussing Ryan’s progress and families. Eventually, the tone shifted, and Ryan’s father looked at Soren with a gaze full of deep gratitude.

"We really cannot thank you enough, Mr. Soren," his father said, his voice thick with emotion. "If you hadn’t been there to save our son, we don’t even want to think about what would have happened to him and our family."
"Yes, you gave our boy a second chance at life," his mother added, nodding in agreement.

Soren finished his food and set his fork down, offering them a reassuring smile. "Please, don’t mention it. I only did what anyone in my position should have done, and I’m just glad Ryan is safe and doing well."
He paused, letting the atmosphere settle, before his expression turned serious. "Actually, I agreed to this meeting today because I wanted to have an important talk with you. It’s about..."

sentences.text: "Don’t worry about that," Soren chuckled softly, completely untroubled by her words.
"As long as you can learn it and benefit from it, that’s completely fine with me.
Besides, the technique is exclusively for females anyway.
I couldn’t use it even if I wanted to."
Ethea fell silent for a brief moment, her eyes fixed on his calm, reassuring face.
A fierce, quiet determination took root deep within her chest as she made a silent vow.
’Then I will just have to develop one for you myself.’
With that silent promise echoing in her mind, a comfortable, lingering warmth finally replaced the chaotic tension in the room.
Across from her, Soren took a sip of tea, his posture fully returning to its usual steady, dependable state, completely unaware of the monumental task his wife had just set for herself.
Modifying or creating a technique from scratch was a feat usually reserved for Emperors or even stronger figures who possessed immense experience.
For someone in her current, crippled state to even attempt it with a legendary-grade heritage technique like the Stellar Soul Weaver Sutra was pure madness.
Yet, Ethea didn’t feel a single shred of doubt.
Well, it’s not like she hasn’t done it before.
With that grounding realization, she let the ambitious thought drift to the back of her mind and relaxed back into her seat as Soren switched the display screen back on to finish the broadcast.
They quietly watched the rest of the program together before he carefully carried her back to the bedroom, bringing a peaceful end to a night that had changed everything between them.
Over the next few days, Soren remained at home, splitting his time between his own training and accompanying Ethea.
The constant proximity naturally shrank the distance between them, melting away the old formal barriers until their daily interactions felt completely effortless.
Yet, a strange new friction quietly took its place.

Whenever he lifted her from her seat or leaned in close to adjust her blankets, his movements would suddenly stall, his hands hovering for a fraction of a second as if he had suddenly forgotten how to breathe.
He found himself tracking the subtle curve of her lips when she smiled, only to abruptly snap his gaze away and clear his throat the moment she caught him looking.

He couldn’t understand why a simple, accidental brush of their fingers now sent a sudden jolt straight to his chest, but the inexplicable awkwardness left him meticulously policing his every move, desperately trying to look normal while hyper-aware of her every breath.
Fortunately, he was finally heading out today.
After his morning appointment, he intended to take some time for himself to clear his head and figure out why his own body was suddenly acting like a broken script around her.
"I’ll be back by dinner, stay safe," Soren said, offering a brief wave to Ethea and Clara before stepping through the front door.
Twenty minutes later, the taxi pulled up outside a modest apartment building situated just a short distance from the city center.
Soren stepped out into the crisp air and lightly stretched his arms, hearing a satisfying pop in his shoulders.
’Perhaps I should just buy a car soon,’ he mused, noting how much time he was spending on commutes lately.
Pulling his phone from his pocket, he glanced at the screen to double-check the address one last time.
Confirming he was at the right place, he slipped the device away, entered the building, and took the stairs.
He maintained a steady pace until he reached the fifth floor, stopping directly in front of the door number listed in his messages, and firmly pressed the doorbell.
A moment later, the door clicked open, and a familiar, youthful face popped out.
"Oh, you’re here, sir!"
"Mmm." Soren offered a nod.
" And I told you, you can just call me Brother Soren, Ryan."
The boy gave an embarrassed nod and quickly stepped aside, gesturing for him to come in.
"Please come inside, we have been waiting for you."
"Excuse me," Soren murmured, stepping over the threshold.
Ryan led him down the short hallway and into the cozy living room, where the rest of his family was gathered.
The moment his sibling and parents noticed his arrival, they immediately stood up from the sofa, their posture straight with a mix of deep respect and nervous anticipation.
They exchanged greetings quickly.
"Please, come in!
It is an honor to have you in our home," Ryan’s father said, stepping forward with an open, welcoming smile to shake Soren’s hand warmly.
"Thank you for having me," Soren replied, returning the firm handshake before exchanging polite greetings with Ryan’s mother and younger sister.
The family eagerly gestured for him to take the most comfortable seat in the living room.
Once everyone had settled down, Ryan’s mother quickly disappeared into the kitchen, returning a moment later with a large, steaming platter of freshly made dumplings.
The savory aroma instantly filled the cozy space.
"You must be hungry after your trip here.
Please, eat up while they are still hot," she urged, placing a fork and a small side dish in front of him.
Soren didn’t stand on ceremony at the sight of one of his favorite meals.
’I guess this is why he asked me about it.’
He chuckled inwardly before taking a bite of a dumpling, the rich, flavorful filling hitting the spot perfectly.
"These are excellent, thank you," he said, genuinely enjoying the meal.
For the next ten or more minutes, they exchanged relaxed small talk, discussing Ryan’s progress and families.
Eventually, the tone shifted, and Ryan’s father looked at Soren with a gaze full of deep gratitude.
"We really cannot thank you enough, Mr.
Soren," his father said, his voice thick with emotion.
"If you hadn’t been there to save our son, we don’t even want to think about what would have happened to him and our family."
"Yes, you gave our boy a second chance at life," his mother added, nodding in agreement.
Soren finished his food and set his fork down, offering them a reassuring smile.
"Please, don’t mention it.
I only did what anyone in my position should have done, and I’m just glad Ryan is safe and doing well."
He paused, letting the atmosphere settle, before his expression turned serious.
"Actually, I agreed to this meeting today because I wanted to have an important talk with you.
It’s about..."

chapters.title: Chapter 108: Party Training [1]
paragraphs: "It’s about Ryan," Soren finished, setting the serious tone for the room. "And his future."
The sudden turn in the conversation brought a flicker of surprise to his father’s eyes, but the older man quickly regained his composure and gave a firm nod. "Go on, Mr. Soren. We are listening."
Soren stole a quick glance at Ryan, catching the way the boy’s shoulders locked up as he waited with bated breath. Turning back to the parents, Soren laid his cards on the table.

"I want to formally recruit Ryan into my party," Soren said, getting straight to the point. "He has incredible potential and possesses a rare kind of strength. Honestly, he was a major reason we even made it out alive back then."

He paused, letting the parents process the weight of his words before addressing their immediate concern. "I know he still has to attend the academy, but I promise you that our work won’t affect his studies. That is why, before taking any steps forward, I wanted to come here and ask for your permission."
A heavy silence settled over the living room as Soren’s words sank in.
Ryan’s parents exchanged a long, complex look, a mixture of pride, anxiety, and profound hesitation flashing between them.
Ryan himself looked like he was about to burst from the suspense, his knuckles whitening as he gripped his knees, waiting for his father’s verdict.
Finally, Ryan’s father let out a slow, measured breath and turned his gaze back to Soren.

"Mr. Soren, we trust you deeply. If it weren’t for you, Ryan wouldn’t even be sitting here today," the older man began, his voice steady but laced with a father’s natural worry. "But as parents, our first instinct is always to keep him safe. The world out there... It’s getting more dangerous by the day."
He paused, glancing over at his son, who looked up with nervous but hopeful eyes.

"However," the father continued, a faint, resigned smile appearing on his face, "we also know our boy. Ever since that day, he hasn’t stopped training or talking about wanting to grow stronger so he can protect us and help people, just like you did. If he stays under our wings forever, he will never achieve his full potential."

Ryan’s mother reached over, placing a supportive hand over her husband’s before looking at Soren with deep earnestness. "As long as you promise to look out for him, and as long as he keeps his grades up, you have our permission."
Before Soren could even open his mouth to reply, Ryan burst out in sheer joy, the built-up tension vanishing instantly.
"Thank you, Father! Thank you, Mother!" he exclaimed, his face lighting up as he stood up and bowed deeply to both of them, his voice thick with excitement and gratitude.

Soren watched the scene silently, a faint, warm smile touching his lips as he let the family share the emotional moment and calm down. Once Ryan finally sat back down, still grinning from ear to ear, Soren looked at the young man.

"Congratulations, Ryan. Welcome to the team," Soren said, before turning back to the parents with a respectful nod. "And thank you both for trusting me. I give you my word that I will look out for him and ensure he returns home safely after every mission."

They sat together for a while longer, the heavy atmosphere completely lifting as they chatted about the upcoming schedule and relaxed. When the time came to wrap up the meeting, Soren stood up from the sofa to take his leave.
Ryan’s father escorted him toward the exit.
Just as they reached the door, Ryan’s mother quickly hurried out of the kitchen holding a neatly packed, insulated food container.
"Mr. Soren, please take this with you," she said warmly, pressing the box into his hands. "It’s a fresh batch of dumplings for your wife. Make sure she eats them while they are fresh."
Soren blinked in surprise, then chuckled softly as he gripped the container. "Thank you, she will definitely love these."
Setting his gaze on the boy, who was already waiting outside, Soren asked. "You ready?"
"Yes, Brother Soren!" Ryan replied, giving a firm, resolute nod.

After bidding a warm farewell to the parents and his younger sister, the two of them stepped out of the apartment and left the building together, ready to take their first real step as an official party.
An hour later, they arrived at their destination, the Greenfang Cave, a standard First Circle Gate on the outskirts of the city.

After clearing the checkpoint and verifying their permits, the two of them stopped directly in front of the swirling vortex. They exchanged a brief glance and a nod before stepping through the threshold together.
Stepping through the portal, they saw the concrete streets vanish beneath their boots, replaced by the uneven, jagged floor of a vast underground cave.

Fortunately, they didn’t have to walk far before the echoes of cackling and shuffling feet reached their ears. Emerging from a bend in the tunnel was a scouting pack of five goblins, clutching crude daggers and rusted clubs. As First Circle monsters, they were weak, making them the ideal targets for two Peak Second Circle combatants looking to test something new.
Soren unclasped his spear, letting the weapon slide naturally into his grip as he took a forward stance. Beside him, Ryan drew his sword, the ring of the blade sharp against the stone walls.
"Match my wavelength," Soren murmured.
"Got it," Ryan replied, his focus sharpening instantly.
As the goblins shrieked and rushed forward, the two executed the Dual Eclipse Arts.

Soren stepped into the vanguard, acting as the immutable anchor. He met the initial rush head-on, his spear thrusting with heavy, calculated precision to block the path and absorb the enemy’s momentum. The blunt force of his strikes easily deflected their crude weapons, drawing all the goblins’ chaotic aggression squarely onto himself.

The moment the monsters overextended, Ryan moved. Operating as the fluid striker, he glided past Soren’s flank, his timing perfectly mirroring Soren’s positioning. Exploiting the wide openings left by the deflected attacks, Ryan delivered swift, clean slashes that cut through the exposed monsters.
However, there was one tiny problem...
"...They’re dead."
That the monsters died too fast.

chapters.title: Chapter 109: Party Training [2]
paragraphs: "They’re dead..."
Ryan muttered in disappointment, lowering his sword as the last goblin collapsed to the stone floor.
The entire engagement had lasted barely a few seconds, leaving them absolutely no room to actually practice the finer details of the blueprint.
Soren looked down at the fallen monsters and nodded slowly, leaning his spear against his shoulder. "I guess we are just much stronger than First Circle monsters now."

He didn’t seem to mind the anticlimactic result, though. Turning his gaze deeper into the dark tunnel, he gave the boy a reassuring slap on the shoulder. "Let’s keep moving. It’s much safer to work out the kinks here than to risk making a mistake in a Second Circle gate. We’ll find a bigger horde or just practice on the Boss."
Ryan nodded in agreement, his disappointment quickly fading as he took a breath and centered his focus.
As they stepped over the fallen goblins and ventured deeper into the winding cavern, Soren paused internally, a sudden, fleeting thought causing him to look down at his hands.
He couldn’t help but realize how incredibly arrogant he must have sounded just now.
A few short weeks ago, he was a nobody struggling just to survive against basic slimes.
Now, he was casually dismissing an entire pack of Gate monsters as mere practice material, talking about clearing a boss room just to run a diagnostic on a new technique.
A faint, wry smile touched his lips, and he shook his head to clear the thought.
Yet, looking at the blood on his spear, the irony faded into a simple statement of fact.
This wasn’t arrogance.
It was the grounded, undeniable confidence that came straight from his rapid growth and the sheer power flowing through his veins.
He had earned every bit of this strength, and it was only logical to acknowledge the reality of where he stood now.
Accepting that progress meant putting it to use. With a renewed focus, Soren picked up his pace, Ryan stepping smoothly into rhythm right beside him.
And so, over the next half hour, the Greenfang Cave became nothing more than a proving ground.
Every subsequent pack of goblins that rushed them from the shadows met a swift end, turning the clearing process into a brisk, uninterrupted walk.
By the time they reached the heavy wooden barricade guarding the deepest chamber, the repetition had allowed them to iron out the basic positioning of their new style.
Stepping past the shattered remains of the barricade, they finally met their true target: the Goblin Chief.

Unlike its smaller kin, this creature stood about seven feet tall, its muscular grey hide covered in scarred leather armor. It wielded a massive, jagged cleaver with practiced ease, its yellow eyes tracking their entrance with a cold, predatory intelligence. Sensing the threat, it threw back its head and let out a guttural roar, its chest swelling as a deep, crimson aura flared around its body.
Instantly, a heavy pressure flooded the chamber, activating its inherent ability: Chieftain’s Domination.
The aura acted as a localized gravity field, forcing a heavy, crushing weight on anyone who stepped within its radius, restricting their movements.
Soren felt his own innate resistance flare, ready to naturally nullify the negative effect. Instead, he consciously suppressed it, choosing to experience the full weight of the pressure.
"Maintain your center," Soren directed, his voice steady as he stepped directly into the crimson zone. "This is exactly what we need. Lock the synchronization."
Ryan’s boots ground into the dirt, his jaw clenched as he adjusted to the sudden, oppressive force, but his eyes remained locked on the target.

The Goblin Chief didn’t just charge blindly. It closed the distance with deliberate, heavy strides, using the crushing gravity to test their reactions before launching a brutal, feinted overhead strike. Mid-swing, the monster altered its trajectory, snapping the massive cleaver into a devastating horizontal arc meant to cleave both of them at once.
Soren planted his feet firmly against the crushing pull, and his spear snapped forward to intercept the giant blade.
Clang!

The ring of metal on metal echoed violently through the cave. Soren absorbed the entire kinetic impact, his stance unyielding as he channeled the force straight into the ground, completely stalling the Chief’s momentum.
The monster’s eyes widened slightly in surprise as its weapon was halted, and it immediately tried to rip the cleaver back to reset its guard.

But the opening was already there. Ryan slipped around Soren’s flank like a shadow, using his partner’s rigid position to shield himself from the worst of the gravity field. Matching Soren’s breathing perfectly, Ryan accelerated through the dense air. His sword flashed upwards in a clean, vertical arc, slicing deep through the thick hide of the monster’s exposed torso.

The Goblin Chief snarled, stumbling back a step as dark blood welled from the chest wound. It immediately raised its cleaver, expecting the intruders to rush forward to finish the kill. Instead, it saw the smaller enemy smoothly step back behind the big one.
The Chief blinked, its yellow eyes darting between the two. It became confused since they weren’t attacking or running away. They were just standing there.
"Again. Watch the transition when it resets." The big one spoke.
"Right." The smaller one replied.
Irritated by their stillness, the Chief roared and lunged again.

It swung from the left, only for the spear to perfectly intercept the blow with a jarring ring of steel. It immediately followed up with a brutal downward hack, but the spear met it effortlessly, absorbing the entire impact. Every single time the massive cleaver clashed against that unyielding wall, the smaller enemy would glide past, his sword flashing out to leave a precise, stinging cut on the Chief’s arms or flanks before retreating.
Two more clashes passed, then three.
Slowly, the monster’s predatory mind sensed something deeply wrong.
The intruders...
They were toying with it!
To a ruler of the cave, being treated as nothing more than an object to test themselves against was an intolerable insult.
The Chief’s composure completely shattered.
"KHRAAAAGH!"
It let out a deafening, furious screech, its crimson aura flaring violently as it abandoned all caution.
"GURRRK!"

It threw its entire weight forward, swinging the massive cleaver in a frenzied, chaotic storm of strikes. The heavy blade tore through the air, leaving red afterimages as it smashed against the stone floor, spraying debris everywhere.
Yet, no matter how wild or powerful the onslaught became, it couldn’t breach their defense.

Whenever the heavy cleaver threatened to overwhelm them, Soren met the attack head-on. His spear deflected the brutal downward hacks, acting as an unbreakable shield that absorbed the raw kinetic energy of the furious monster.
And every time the Chief overextended or left its flanks exposed during its blind rage, Ryan’s sword flashed through the gaps, leaving precise, shallow cuts that further drained the beast’s stamina.

They moved in a continuous, rhythmic loop: block, slip, counter, reset. With every passing minute, the heavy friction of the Chieftain’s Domination felt less like a restriction and more like a natural backdrop to their movements.
Their synchronization grew tighter, the lag between Soren’s deflections and Ryan’s strikes narrowing down to a fraction of a second.
Eventually, the violent storm began to slow.

The crimson gravity field flickered and waned as the Goblin Chief’s breaths turned into ragged, desperate gasps. Its massive shoulders heaved, its muscular arms trembling under the weight of its own weapon.

Finally, with one last, pathetic swing that completely missed Soren, the giant monster lost its footing. The cleaver clattered uselessly to the ground, and the Chief collapsed heavily onto its knees, utterly exhausted, staring up at them with a mixture of rage, fear, and pure defeat.

Soren lowered his spear, his breathing entirely controlled. Beside him, Ryan stood steady, his blade resting at his side without a hint of the initial rush. They had taken everything the boss had to offer and used it to cement the foundation of their art.
"Good job," Soren said quietly, looking down at the defeated creature. "Let’s put it out of its misery."
Ryan nodded, stepping forward with a calm, disciplined stride to deliver the final, merciful strike.

Yet, no matter how wild or powerful the onslaught became, it couldn’t breach their defense.
Whenever the heavy cleaver threatened to overwhelm them, Soren met the attack head-on.
His spear deflected the brutal downward hacks, acting as an unbreakable shield that absorbed the raw kinetic energy of the furious monster.
And every time the Chief overextended or left its flanks exposed during its blind rage, Ryan’s sword flashed through the gaps, leaving precise, shallow cuts that further drained the beast’s stamina.
They moved in a continuous, rhythmic loop: block, slip, counter, reset.
With every passing minute, the heavy friction of the Chieftain’s Domination felt less like a restriction and more like a natural backdrop to their movements.
Their synchronization grew tighter, the lag between Soren’s deflections and Ryan’s strikes narrowing down to a fraction of a second.
Eventually, the violent storm began to slow.
The crimson gravity field flickered and waned as the Goblin Chief’s breaths turned into ragged, desperate gasps.
Its massive shoulders heaved, its muscular arms trembling under the weight of its own weapon.
Finally, with one last, pathetic swing that completely missed Soren, the giant monster lost its footing.
The cleaver clattered uselessly to the ground, and the Chief collapsed heavily onto its knees, utterly exhausted, staring up at them with a mixture of rage, fear, and pure defeat.
Soren lowered his spear, his breathing entirely controlled.
Beside him, Ryan stood steady, his blade resting at his side without a hint of the initial rush.
They had taken everything the boss had to offer and used it to cement the foundation of their art.
"Good job," Soren said quietly, looking down at the defeated creature.
"Let’s put it out of its misery."
Ryan nodded, stepping forward with a calm, disciplined stride to deliver the final, merciful strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 110: Novice No. 2’s Dilemmas
paragraphs: Swoosh-!
Ryan delivered the final strike, putting the creature down.
They quickly harvested the mana core from the corpse, gathered the valuable materials, and left the gate.
Now that they were done smurfing in a First Circle gate, they left the outpost without wasting any time.

They caught a transit ride across the city outskirts and headed straight toward their actual destination: the Muddy Burrow, a Second Circle Gate where they could finally test their teamwork much more thoroughly.
Even though they could probably clear a Third Circle Gate if they gave it their all, just like their desperate survival inside the Golden Gate, choosing a Second Circle one was the right call.

First, they didn’t have much of a choice anyway. Soren was still officially an E-rank hunter registered at the Second Circle level. Ryan was still a student, and he was keeping his breakthrough to the Third Circle a closely guarded secret. In fact, Soren had only found out about it today, and Ryan asked him to keep it a secret. Because of these restrictions, they were completely unable to book or enter a Third Circle Gate through official channels.

Secondly, they were still a small party of two. Having recently recovered from their near-death experiences, neither of them was eager to risk their lives again so soon. Jumping straight into higher-tier gates with an untested partnership was a recipe for disaster.

And finally, a Second Circle gate provided the ideal threshold for steady refinement. The monsters here would be aggressive enough to actively push their new style without completely overwhelming them if a mistake occurred. They didn’t need life-or-death stakes to make progress; they just needed an environment where they could actually push the pace.
As the transport sped toward the burrow, the dark silhouette of the reinforced gate outpost loomed in the distance.
They swiped their entry permits at the automated terminal, completed the brief security scan, and stepped directly into the distortion field without a second thought.
Two hours later, they walked back out through the swirling vortex completely unscathed.

The Muddy Burrow had thrown everything a standard Second Circle gate could muster at them, from aggressive burrowing beasts to a heavy, swarming boss, but their synchronized style held up perfectly. They managed to smooth out the transition gaps in their technique until the movements became almost instinctual.
Standing outside the outpost lobby, Soren divided the harvested cores and materials into two equal shares and handed Ryan his portion.
With the day’s objective thoroughly accomplished and the blueprint successfully tested, they exchanged a brief nod and parted ways, each heading back to their respective destinations.
Since he was already in Eastern Kalmira for the raid, Soren decided to stop by the Verdant Glen Gardens, using the opportunity to sort out his thoughts before heading home.

He caught a local transit pod that dropped him off right at the edge of the district’s ecological zone. Stepping off the platform, he passed through the grand arched entrance of the gardens, the sudden shift from the bustling city streets to the serene expanse immediately easing the tension in his shoulders.
The garden was remarkably quiet today, with only the occasional automated maintenance drone humming softly in the distance as it trimmed the hedges.
Soren let his feet guide him down the winding stone paths, breathing in the crisp, floral-infused air.
As he rounded a familiar corridor of white wisteria arches, his gaze fell upon a quiet wooden pavilion. It was the exact spot where he and Ethea had sat together during their walk.
The sudden memory of her quiet presence made the path’s current emptiness feel much more pronounced, and Soren lingered by the arches for a moment, his eyes fixed on the empty wooden bench.
’I really came all the way out here to escape the tension, yet she’s still the first thing I think about,’ he thought, a faint, wry smile crossing his face.
Shaking his head at his own helplessness, he turned away from the pavilion to find some actual privacy.

He ambled deeper into the sanctuary until he reached a secluded spot near a large, clear pond. Sitting down on a stone bench, he leaned forward and stared at his own reflection stretching across the still water.
"Oh, I got a bit more handsome, huh?"
He chuckled lightly at the thought.

It wasn’t just a baseless boast, though. His facial features had significantly sharpened, losing the gaunt, hollow look of his survival days, and his posture carried a natural presence. His eyes became clearer and more profound, carrying a subtle, piercing depth that naturally commanded attention.

This transformation wasn’t a mere coincidence; it was the direct result of his awakening, the constant refinement of cultivation, and training. The pure mana circulating through his meridians had systematically purged the impurities from his body, reshaping his physique and lending an effortless, steady composure to his every movement.
Soren squinted.

If he actually bothered to visit a professional styling salon instead of settling for his usual low-maintenance look, and if he traded his plain clothes and utilitarian hunter gear for a decent tailored outfit, he could probably give those arrogant, trust-fund young masters or top-tier idol actors a serious run for their money.
Heck, if he continues to sharpen his presence at this rate, he might even make a few of them look like background extras.

’Not that it matters anyway,’ he mused, tilting his head slightly as he examined his watery image. ’It’s not like I’m planning to audition for a romance drama or win a modeling contest. Who am I even trying to impress?’
The answer surfaced in his mind before he could stop it, instantly making his smug amusement wither away.
As the faint smile died on his lips, his gaze drifted deeper into the shimmering water, and his thoughts naturally gravitated back toward the small apartment.
The lighthearted mood evaporated, replaced by a sudden, familiar tightness in his chest.
’Haha...’
It was ridiculous, really.

He could stand perfectly still inside a dangerous gate, talk and deal with an otherworldly emperor, face down charging beasts, and calculate split-second deflections without a single tremor in his hands.
And yet...
A single, soft memory from a quiet bedroom was all it took to completely bypass his defenses.
’Urgh...’

chapters.title: Chapter 111: Novice No. 2’s Promotion
paragraphs: ’..Urgh.’
The moment his mind replayed the gentle, flushed expression on Ethea’s face, the absolute determination in her eyes when she called him her husband, his entire system completely glitched.

He could still vividly recall the exact weight of the silence that followed, the frantic, loud hammering of his own ribs, and the sheer terror of not knowing how to look at her without giving himself away.
’I’m completely hopeless...’
He rested his elbows on his knees, burying his face in his hands with a quiet, defeated groan.

He stayed like that for a long time, the cool air of the gardens brushing past him, doing absolutely nothing to put out the sudden heat flare in his face. It took a few deep, deliberate breaths to finally force his racing pulse back down to a manageable rhythm. Slowly lowering his hands, he looked back at the pond, his expression turning serious.
He couldn’t deny it anymore.
This wasn’t just the lingering awkwardness of a sudden conversation; it was a total internal shift.
Looking back, he realized he had been treating their entire living arrangement like a high-stakes tactical mission.

He also had spent the past few days constantly trying to rationalize his actions, convincing himself that his hyper-awareness was just a natural part of being a diligent protector, a good husband. He had filed every cooked meal, every shared conversation, and every lingering glance under the safe, comfortable label of responsibility and duty.
’...No, this wasn’t just because of duty...’

Duty didn’t make a man’s heart hammer violently against his ribs just because their fingers accidentally brushed while adjusting a blanket. Duty didn’t cause him to meticulously police his every movement, terrified that she would catch him tracking the subtle curve of her lips whenever she smiled.
The reason was far simpler, yet infinitely more terrifying.
’Could it be...’
Staring back down at his reflection in the pond, his breath hitched.
’Could it be that I...?’

The water rippled slightly as a gentle breeze blew across the garden, blurring his features just like the chaotic emotions blurring his logic. The denial he had been clinging to for days finally crumbled under the weight of his own racing pulse.
’I... I’ve fallen for her?’
Soren fell silent.
His mind went entirely blank as he stared unblinkingly at his reflection, the chaotic rush of his previous thoughts suddenly dying out.
’I have fallen for her... fallen... fallen...’
The words continued to ring in his head like a stone dropped into still water, sending quiet tremors through everything he thought he understood about himself.
Automatically, his mind tried to scramble for a rebuttal. He desperately reached for any logical alternative, wanting to prove to himself that he was simply overcomplicating things.
Perhaps he was just wrong.
Sure, he liked her. He enjoyed her company, felt a protective instinct toward her, and genuinely cared about her well-being.
But love? Real, actual love?
That was a massive leap. It was a completely foreign concept, something entirely outside the scope of his reality.
He waited for his brain to find a loophole, to present a convincing counterargument that would restore his usual pragmatism.
There was no loophole. There was no clever workaround or misinterpretation.
He closed his eyes for a brief second, and when he opened them, the truth was the only thing left.
’I’ve really fallen for her.’
A soft, helpless chuckle bubbled up in his throat, a faint sound that carried more disbelief than actual amusement.
He let out a slow breath, watching the pond’s surface gradually resettle into a clear, undisturbed mirror.
Strangely, the suffocating tightness that had been squeezing his chest completely disappeared.
In its place, a strange sense of peace and unexpected sweetness began to bloom, settling deep into his bones and making the heavy burden of his thoughts feel surprisingly manageable.
How exactly had this even happened?
He searched his memory for a single, defining turning point, a specific moment where the line had been crossed, but he came up entirely empty-handed.
As for that night... It was probably when he actually noticed the shift within himself, rather than the exact moment the feeling was born.

There was no love at first sight, nor some sudden, grand event that changed everything between them. It had been more gradual. The emotion had simply accumulated over time, building up quietly through a thousand unnoticed details until it finally overflowed.
Soren rested his chin on his palm, letting his gaze drift as the timeline finally began to make sense.

He went from treating her as someone he had promised to protect and care for to someone whose opinion mattered more than anything else. He actually liked coming home to her. He liked the quiet routine they had built, and the mere idea of her looking at someone else the way she looked at him made an ugly, possessive knot tie itself in his stomach.
He wasn’t just invested in her safety or recovery anymore; he was completely invested in her.
He pressed his thumb against his temple, his features tightening again as the relief of finally being honest with himself gave way to a much trickier problem.
Admitting his own feelings to himself was one thing. But...
What about Ethea?
The question lingered in the air, bringing with it a sudden, sharp edge of uncertainty.
When she had looked him dead in the eye and promised to fulfill her role as his wife, her cheeks flushing a soft, lovely pink... had it truly been out of affection?
Or was it just an overwhelming sense of gratitude for everything he had done to protect her?
Ethea...
How did she even feel about him?
As far as he knew, Ethea was a proud, fiercely independent figure, regardless of her current physical limitations.
He had saved her life, sheltered her, and provided a safe haven when she was at her most vulnerable.

It wouldn’t be surprising if her sudden openness was just her way of trying to repay the immense debt she felt she owed him. She had explicitly stated she wanted to master the technique so she wouldn’t be a burden anymore after all.
’She also said to fulfill her role...’
