chapters.title: Chapter 112: Theory and Practice
paragraphs: ’She also said ’to fulfill her role’...’
Not because she wanted to, but because she felt she had to. Just like him back then. That’s exactly why...
’It would be pretty arrogant to assume she’s actually in love with me.’
The realization brought a faint, self-deprecating smile to his lips. He picked up a small pebble from the path and tossed it into the water, shattering his reflection entirely.
As the ripples faded, he shook his head, forcing his thoughts to stop spiraling.

There was no point in overanalyzing it. Whether she was acting out of deep gratitude or a strict sense of marital duty, the reality of their daily life wasn’t going to change overnight. She was still recovering, he was still trying to grow stronger, and they both had a long way to go.

He would just keep doing what he had always done: protecting her, supporting her, and letting whatever was growing between them take its own natural course. He wouldn’t force it, and he wouldn’t let his own sudden realization make things awkward between them.
With his mind finally settled, Soren stood up from the stone bench, stretched his arms, and turned back toward the path.
It was time to head home.
[Some time later.]
The heavy electronic lock released with a soft click. Soren stepped into the quiet foyer, carefully sealing the door behind him before making his way toward the main living area.
As he rounded the corner, Ethea’s gaze shifted smoothly toward the entrance, her eyes locking onto him the exact moment he came into view.
Soren froze for a fraction of a second, his foot hovering just over the edge of the floor.

The moment his eyes met hers, his brain completely blanked on the casual greeting he had practiced three times on the way up the stairs. His gaze dropped entirely on instinct, tracking the slight movement of her fingers, then darting away before he could accidentally stare at her lips.
A wry chuckle escaped his throat, a breathless sound directed entirely at his own pathetic display.
’...I guess talking and doing is entirely different, huh.’
His resolve hadn’t even survived the walk from the doorway.
It was a complete disaster.
Despite acknowledging his feelings by the pond and firmly deciding not to make things weird, he couldn’t just switch his brain off.
In fact, now that the truth was out in the open, pretending became ten times harder.
Before, his ignorance had acted like a shield; he could blame his racing pulse on situational awareness or adrenaline. Now, every single glance was a conscious choice, and every choice felt heavy.
He couldn’t even look her in the eye without a sudden heat creeping up his neck.
Every natural instinct he possessed had completely abandoned him.
Since casual acting was entirely out of the question, his only choice was to lean heavily into the one persona that always worked when his brain was compromised: absolute, rigid professionalism.
"I’m back," Soren said, his voice coming out a little stiffer than usual.
To keep his hands busy, he immediately set his jacket down, folding it over the back of a nearby chair with unnecessary precision.
"Are you alright?" Ethea asked, perhaps noticing his stiff posture.
Soren paused, his hand still on his jacket. He cleared his throat and offered a quick, strained smile. "No, everything’s okay. Just a little tired from the raid, that’s all."
Ethea looked at him with clear suspicion, but she didn’t press the issue.
Hoping to change the subject, Soren recalled something he arranged in the morning. "Ah, right! Did the dumplings arrive?"
Ethea’s expression softened at the mention of the food, and she nodded gently. "Yes. They were actually very delicious. The wrapper was thin, and the filling was perfectly seasoned."
"Right?" Soren agreed, a more genuine, relaxed smile finally breaking through his rigid mask. "I knew you’d like them. It was actually Ryan’s mother who made sure I took them. She’s really kind."

Before Ethea could respond, the sound of light footsteps approached from the kitchen area. Aunt Clara walked out into the living room, wiping her hands on a small towel as a warm smile lit up her face.
"Welcome back, Soren," Clara greeted him cheerfully. "We were just talking about when you would come back."
"Aunt Clara," Soren greeted her with a small nod, feeling a massive wave of relief at the timely interruption.
Seizing the perfect chance to escape before his composure could slip any further, he pointed toward the hallway. "I’m going to wash up first."
Without waiting for a reply, he quickly took his leave, practically retreating down the wide hallway toward the washroom to get some distance and finally breathe.
Aunt Clara and Ethea exchanged a brief, confused glance as the bathroom door clicked shut down the hall.
"He must be really tired," Aunt Clara remarked, breaking the silence with a soft sigh. Deciding to give him the benefit of the doubt, she shook her head gently. "He recovered not long ago too."

Ethea looked toward the empty hallway, humming a quiet note of agreement. She didn’t voice her lingering doubts, but she couldn’t shake the feeling that his sudden stiffness had very little to do with physical exhaustion.

Thankfully, a blast of freezing water did exactly what it was supposed to do. By the time he stepped out, dried off, and changed into comfortable indoor clothes, he was much better at handling himself.

He managed to navigate the rest of the evening without a single slip-up. During dinner, he kept his focus on casual, lighthearted topics, successfully maintaining his professional, steady persona through sheer force of will.
The strategy worked perfectly. Right up until this exact moment.
Soren stood at the edge of the master bedroom, the ambient lighting casting long shadows across the floor did absolutely nothing to ease the sudden tension locking up his joints.
He gulped inwardly, his gaze shifting from the edge of the neatly made bed down to Ethea.
It was time for her to rest, which meant he had to lift her.

His eyes locked onto her slender shoulders, then tracked down to where his hands would have to rest to support her weight properly. A sudden, glaring realization hit him, making his throat feel completely dry.
’...Just how did I do this until now?’

His gaze dropped entirely on instinct, tracking the slight movement of her fingers, then darting away before he could accidentally stare at her lips.
A wry chuckle escaped his throat, a breathless sound directed entirely at his own pathetic display.
’...I guess talking and doing is entirely different, huh.’
His resolve hadn’t even survived the walk from the doorway.
It was a complete disaster.
Despite acknowledging his feelings by the pond and firmly deciding not to make things weird, he couldn’t just switch his brain off.
In fact, now that the truth was out in the open, pretending became ten times harder.
Before, his ignorance had acted like a shield; he could blame his racing pulse on situational awareness or adrenaline.
Now, every single glance was a conscious choice, and every choice felt heavy.
He couldn’t even look her in the eye without a sudden heat creeping up his neck.
Every natural instinct he possessed had completely abandoned him.
Since casual acting was entirely out of the question, his only choice was to lean heavily into the one persona that always worked when his brain was compromised: absolute, rigid professionalism.
"I’m back," Soren said, his voice coming out a little stiffer than usual.
To keep his hands busy, he immediately set his jacket down, folding it over the back of a nearby chair with unnecessary precision.
"Are you alright?" Ethea asked, perhaps noticing his stiff posture.
Soren paused, his hand still on his jacket.
He cleared his throat and offered a quick, strained smile.
"No, everything’s okay.
Just a little tired from the raid, that’s all."
Ethea looked at him with clear suspicion, but she didn’t press the issue.
Hoping to change the subject, Soren recalled something he arranged in the morning.
"Ah, right!
Did the dumplings arrive?"
Ethea’s expression softened at the mention of the food, and she nodded gently.
"Yes.
They were actually very delicious.
The wrapper was thin, and the filling was perfectly seasoned."
"Right?" Soren agreed, a more genuine, relaxed smile finally breaking through his rigid mask.
"I knew you’d like them.
It was actually Ryan’s mother who made sure I took them.
She’s really kind."
Before Ethea could respond, the sound of light footsteps approached from the kitchen area.
Aunt Clara walked out into the living room, wiping her hands on a small towel as a warm smile lit up her face.
"Welcome back, Soren," Clara greeted him cheerfully.
"We were just talking about when you would come back."
"Aunt Clara," Soren greeted her with a small nod, feeling a massive wave of relief at the timely interruption.
Seizing the perfect chance to escape before his composure could slip any further, he pointed toward the hallway.
"I’m going to wash up first."
Without waiting for a reply, he quickly took his leave, practically retreating down the wide hallway toward the washroom to get some distance and finally breathe.
Aunt Clara and Ethea exchanged a brief, confused glance as the bathroom door clicked shut down the hall.
"He must be really tired," Aunt Clara remarked, breaking the silence with a soft sigh.
Deciding to give him the benefit of the doubt, she shook her head gently.
"He recovered not long ago too."
Ethea looked toward the empty hallway, humming a quiet note of agreement.
She didn’t voice her lingering doubts, but she couldn’t shake the feeling that his sudden stiffness had very little to do with physical exhaustion.
Thankfully, a blast of freezing water did exactly what it was supposed to do.
By the time he stepped out, dried off, and changed into comfortable indoor clothes, he was much better at handling himself.
He managed to navigate the rest of the evening without a single slip-up.
During dinner, he kept his focus on casual, lighthearted topics, successfully maintaining his professional, steady persona through sheer force of will.
The strategy worked perfectly.
Right up until this exact moment.
Soren stood at the edge of the master bedroom, the ambient lighting casting long shadows across the floor did absolutely nothing to ease the sudden tension locking up his joints.
He gulped inwardly, his gaze shifting from the edge of the neatly made bed down to Ethea.
It was time for her to rest, which meant he had to lift her.
His eyes locked onto her slender shoulders, then tracked down to where his hands would have to rest to support her weight properly.
A sudden, glaring realization hit him, making his throat feel completely dry.
’...Just how did I do this until now?’

chapters.title: Chapter 113: Sister’s Visit
paragraphs: ’...Whatever. Let’s just do it as I remember.’
Soren took a slow, silent breath, forcing his body to move on pure muscle memory. He stepped forward, bent down, and carefully slid one arm behind her back and the other beneath her knees.

The instant he lifted her, the reality of her proximity hit him full force, but he locked his jaw and moved with mechanical precision. He carried her the short distance and placed her gently onto the mattress. Bending over slightly, he reached for the blanket and pulled it up over her shoulders, keeping his movements as steady and natural as possible.
"...Soren."

Her low voice cut through the quiet room, causing him to freeze instantly, his fingers still gripping the edge of the blanket. He forced his expression to remain entirely neutral before looking up to meet her eyes.
"What is it?" he asked, keeping his tone calm.
Ethea looked up at him, a trace of hesitation flickering across her face. Her lips parted slightly as if she were about to say something important, but after a brief pause, she lowered her gaze.
"...No. Just... goodnight."
"Mm. Goodnight," Soren replied softly, adjusting the edge of the blanket one last time. "Have a nice dream."

He carefully stepped away from the bedside, walking over to where his own mattress was laid out on the floor. As he lay down, the lingering silence in the room felt heavier than usual. He could tell she had wanted to say something else, but since she had chosen to drop it, he decided not to push. He would just wait until she was ready.
Taking a deep breath to clear his mind of the tension, Soren closed his eyes and immediately dove back into his cultivation.
He couldn’t afford to waste a single night. Despite his steady growth, his progress was still a bit slow. Even Ryan had already left him behind, and the gap wasn’t going to close itself.

As mana began to circulate through his core, the quiet warmth of the room faded, replaced by the rigid focus of a man who knew exactly how much stronger he needed to become in order to achieve his purpose.
Two days later.
The sudden chime of the doorbell echoed through the apartment.
At the dining table, Aunt Clara gripped the armrests, ready to stand, but Soren reacted faster.
"I’ll get it," he said, pushing his chair back.
He glanced at the clock; it was about time.
He walked over to the foyer and pulled the door open.
As expected, a familiar face was waiting outside, a beautiful woman with striking white hair.
"Good evening, Sister Zoe," Soren said, stepping back to clear the entryway. "Come on in. We’ve been waiting for you."
"Evening, Soren," Zoe greeted him back, stepping inside the apartment.

She then followed Soren into the living room, her eyes immediately finding Ethea and Aunt Clara. After exchanging brief, polite greetings, Soren guided her to the dining table, pulling out a chair for her before taking his own seat.
As they settled in, the atmosphere became relaxed.
"Miss Ethea," Zoe directed her attention across the table. "How have you been lately? Are you adjusting to the new place well?"
Ethea met her gaze, offering a soft nod. "Sister Zoe. I am doing well, and the new place is much more comfortable. Thank you for your assistance in securing this place."

Zoe waved her hand dismissively, brushing off the gratitude. "I merely pulled a few strings. Soren earned this place through his own merits, so you should thank him instead." She then turned her gaze toward the older woman. "What about you, Aunt Clara? Have you been keeping well too? I hope Soren hasn’t been making your job too difficult."

Clara let out a soft laugh, shaking her head. "Not at all, Lady Zoe. Soren is a wonderful young man. He constantly lends a hand with the household chores, even though that is supposed to be my responsibility."

"Oh, is that so?" Zoe murmured, a subtle, amused glint appearing in her eyes. She glanced back at Soren before looking at the two women again. "Well, if he ever gives you trouble, don’t hesitate to reach out to me. I will discipline him myself. That goes for you too, Miss Ethea. If he ever makes you upset or brings you to tears, just give me a call. I’ll gladly give him a personal crash course on how to treat a woman."
Ethea and Clara both laughed at the remark, the tension in the room melting away completely.
’...’ Soren, however, felt his lips twitch before he let out a helpless sigh.

He could only blame himself for this. Because of his follow-up training sessions to refine the spear technique, their relationship had naturally improved, growing into a comfortable familiarity. Still, he hadn’t anticipated her jumping straight into full teasing mode the moment she stepped through his door.
Shaking his head, he decided it was best to retreat before she could escalate things any further.
He pushed his chair back and stood up from the table.
"You ladies continue talking," he rolled up his sleeves slightly as he turned toward the kitchen. "I’ll take care of the meal."
Zoe paused mid-laugh, her gaze shifting from the two women back to him.
"Wait."
A single eyebrow crept upward with clear doubt.
"...You are the chef?"
Soren simply smiled. "Yes, I can-"
"Hey!" Before he could even finish his sentence, Zoe turned away from him entirely, addressing the other two women. "Is that true? Can he really cook?"
’...There she goes again.’ Soren shook his head, utterly defeated by her relentless teasing.
He didn’t bother arguing, turning on his heel to make a swift exit toward the counter.
"Wait, what are you even cooking?" Zoe called out after him, turning around in her chair. "You’re not just frying eggs, right? Do you need help?"
Soren simply waved his hand without looking back, stepping into the kitchen area.
"Just wait and see."

chapters.title: Chapter 114: The Sizzle of the Pan, the Heat of the Table
paragraphs: Standing in front of the counter, Soren washed his hands and surveyed the ingredients laid out before him. The lively chatter from the dining table drifted into the kitchen, a mix of Zoe’s bright voice, Aunt Clara’s polite chuckles, and Ethea’s occasional responses.
’Perhaps I should have invited Ryan too,’ he thought, reaching for a knife.

Being the only guy in the room felt a little weird. It wasn’t that he felt out of place with them; one was his wife, one he treated as an aunt, and the third was a teacher who doubled as an annoying big sister. It was just that against a lineup like that, he had absolutely no backup.
If Ryan had come tonight, he would have at least shared the burden, even if the guy would probably just sit there like an obedient little brother.
A faint smile touched Soren’s lips as he shook his head, cutting through a bunch of fresh greens.
’Let’s just invite him some other time. Alone.’
That was probably for the best anyway.
After all, he had recognized Ethea’s true identity the moment he saw her back at the hospital. He had looked absolutely shell-shocked at the time, staring like his brain had short-circuited.
Fortunately, nobody else had been around except for Ryan’s parents, and Ryan had possessed enough discretion to keep his mouth shut.
Still, ever since that day, he hadn’t stopped bringing her up in their conversations. He even started dropping subtle hints, asking if it would be alright to visit his home and hang out.
’It seems like he’s a fan of hers or something.’
On the other hand, it was actually a bit strange that others hadn’t recognized her.

Sister Zoe obviously knew who she was at their first meeting, and she hadn’t missed a single opportunity to tease him about it during their training sessions. But everyone else - the staff from the Bureau, the hospital workers, even Lady Seria hadn’t batted an eye.
Soren chopped the rare vegetables, pondering the contradiction.

Perhaps Ethea just wasn’t that famous in this specific city, or maybe they simply didn’t pay much attention to the high-profile Hunter world. To them, top-ranking Hunters were probably like distant celebrities on a screen, hard to connect with a real person sitting right in front of them.
’Well, it works out better for us anyway,’ Soren thought, putting the speculation aside.

He fired up the stove and poured a bit of oil into the pan, letting the rhythmic sizzle ground his thoughts. He could worry about arranging a proper introduction for Ryan some other time. For tonight, his immediate mission was simply to survive Zoe’s teasing and prove he could actually cook.
He set a pot of water to boil alongside the pan.

Well, Aunt Clara and Ethea were already well aware of his culinary skills, but Zoe’s cheap provocation had definitely triggered his competitive side. Even if he had fallen right into her trap, he decided to do his absolute best anyway.
After all, when was he going to put these ’hard-earned’ skills to use if not right now?
With renewed focus, Soren began tossing the ingredients into the pan, the savory aroma instantly filling the air.
’Let’s see if you can resist my cooking~’
Meanwhile, at the dining table, the relaxed atmosphere had suddenly heated up, all because of a single question from Zoe.

Leaning forward with her elbows on the table and her chin resting in her palms, Zoe locked her eyes onto Ethea with a mischievous grin. "So, Miss Ethea, now that Soren is out of earshot... how exactly is your love life going with him? Is he as dutiful a husband as he is a student, or does he need a little pushing?"
Clara blinked in surprise, a small, knowing smile tugging at the corners of her lips as she quietly sipped her tea, choosing to remain a silent spectator.

In her opinion, perhaps Ethea was the one who needed that push more than Soren. After all, the young man seemed to have already figured out his own feelings, albeit he was struggling with them, constantly walking on eggshells around his wife.
Whereas Ethea seemed to have those feelings brewing underneath, but simply hadn’t realized them yet.
Clara shifted her gaze toward Ethea, who still looked completely stunned by Zoe’s sudden interrogation.
That dazed expression, the nervous fidgeting of her fingers, the blush coloring her cheeks—all of it was undeniable proof that Clara’s guesses were entirely correct.
She wasn’t indifferent; she was just lost in territory she had never navigated before.
As Clara watched the silence stretch across the table, Ethea finally managed to find her voice under Zoe’s expectant gaze.
"We... We are simply focusing on our current circumstances, Miss Zoe. There hasn’t been... time for such things."
"I see... But..." Zoe leaned in closer, her eyes narrowing with a look of disbelief. "Don’t tell me you haven’t even held hands properly yet?"

"!" Ethea froze completely once more, the blush on her cheeks deepening into a vivid crimson that spread all the way to the tips of her ears. She opened her mouth to argue, but no words came out, her usual stoic composure entirely shattered by the absurdly accurate accusation.
Zoe stared at her, momentarily speechless.
It was genuinely hard to believe that the revered, icy-cold Ice Empress could ever make such a helpless, flustered expression, but being able to see it firsthand made Zoe hum in joy inwardly.
In fact, teasing her was definitely proving to be way better than messing with that guy.
"Oh my," Zoe gasped, her lips curling into a mischievous grin as she tapped her fingers against her cheek. "You really haven’t, have you? You two are actually hopeless."
Ethea quickly bowed her head, using her long hair to shield her burning face from view, completely unable to meet the older woman’s eyes.
Seeing the poor girl pushed to her absolute limit, Clara decided it was finally time to step in. She set her teacup down with a soft click and looked over at the energetic guest.
"Miss Zoe, please stop teasing her."

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Cooking!
paragraphs: Taking a deep breath, Soren finished preparing the foundational ingredients, arranging thick cuts of marbled beef and chopped moon-stalk celery neatly on the counter.
His gaze then swept over the rest of the ingredients.
’...This single meal cost me almost 200,000 credits,’ he thought, his chest tightening slightly at the sheer numbers. ’I absolutely cannot afford to fail this.’
He focused entirely on the workspace before him, letting the lively chatter from the dining room fade into distant background noise.

Cooking with these premium items required extreme precision due to their volatility. A normal chef might just toss everything into a pot, which would let the elemental essence escape into the air. To prevent such a waste, Soren had to use his own mana to coat the ingredients, locking the pure frost energy directly inside them during the heating process.

He began the journey by pouring a precise measure of Winter-Berry oil into the large soup pot. This oil was incredibly dense, capable of withstanding immense heat without burning, which made it the perfect base. Once the oil reached the ideal temperature, he added the marbled beef, letting the rich fat render down perfectly alongside the moon-stalk celery. These rare base ingredients were crucial, as their unique cellular structures would act as the primary sponge for the magical energy later on.

Once the meat and vegetables had seared beautifully and the liquid base had begun to simmer, it was time for the trickiest part of the recipe. He finely sliced a bundle of crisp Glacial Lotus petals. Each stroke of his knife required him to channel a thin layer of mana through the blade to keep the cold energy from leaking onto the board.

With absolute precision, he dropped the petals into the bubbling broth, carefully adding a few drops of Frost-Root extract to finalize the elemental infusion. The moment the extract hit the liquid, a sudden rush of cold threatened to freeze the entire meal solid. Soren immediately swirled the pot, using his mana to distribute the freezing energy evenly.
’Steady now,’ he thought, keeping his fingers perfectly still. ’The heat needs to cook the physical ingredients while my mana binds the elemental energy into the liquid.’

It was a delicate balancing act that demanded absolute concentration, but his hard-earned control allowed him to tame the elemental forces. Once that primary process was done, the volatile energies finally stabilized, blending into perfect harmony.
With the magical infusion successfully bound to the liquid, the rest of the cooking went much more smoothly.
Time passed while the tense tightness in Soren’s shoulders finally began to ease.
Wiping a bead of sweat from his forehead, he left the soup to simmer quietly, allowing the beef to become incredibly tender and the broth to clarify into a perfectly translucent finish.
When the meal finally concluded its long preparation, a deep sense of satisfaction welled up in his chest. The broth remained beautifully clear, radiating a deceptively warm aroma.

He neatly arranged the soup into deep porcelain bowls and placed them onto a large serving tray alongside the other side dishes. Soren smoothed down his apron, took a calming breath to steady his pulse, and walked out to the dining room.
"Dinner is ready," Soren announced, keeping his voice cheerful and professional.
Hearing his voice, Clara quickly stood up from her seat, helping him serve the food by placing the deep porcelain bowls and side dishes onto the table.
As the plates settled, the rich, savory aroma filled the room, carrying a subtle, crisp undertone that made the atmosphere feel instantly refreshing.
Zoe leaned over her bowl, her eyes widening as she took in the sight. She let out an exclamation, a mix of surprise and delight coloring her face.
"Wow, so you really can cook~" Zoe said, looking up at him with a grin. "Even without tasting, I can tell it’s gonna be good just from the smell and look alone."
"Thanks," Soren replied, a faint smile touching his lips.
Before he could sit down, Clara whispered in a low voice.
"...Let me feed Ethea."
Soren paused, his hand hovering over his chair as he looked at them.
"...Alright," He nodded after a pause. ’I was wondering how I should ask her anyway.’

If sister Zoe witnesses him feeding Ethea like that, who knows what kind of relentless teasing he would have to endure for the next month or even year. Aunt Clara’s timely intervention was a blessing in disguise.
Soren pulled his hand back, smoothly sliding into his own seat across from them.
He picked up his utensils, looking around the table at everyone.
"Well then, let’s dig in."
While Clara picked up a porcelain spoon to help Ethea, Zoe eagerly reached for her own bowl.
Taking a sip himself, Soren observed them, his gaze first falling on Ethea.

She was sitting perfectly rigid. Her posture was exceptionally stiff as she looked down at the steaming bowl placed before her. A faint, barely perceptible tension gripped her shoulders, though her expression remained completely unreadable. It seemed like she had been teased by Sister Zoe a lot before he came.
"Here," Clara scooped a small portion of the translucent broth, blowing on it gently to cool the rising steam before offering it to her.
Ethea leaned forward slightly, accepting the spoonful of soup with quiet grace.

The moment the liquid touched her tongue, Zoe was already digging into her own portion across the table. She picked up a thick piece of the tender meat along with a spoonful of the broth, practically inhaling it.

"Oh my god," She mumbled around her mouthful, her eyes widening to the size of saucers. She swallowed quickly, slamming her spoon back down onto the table. "Soren, what did you even put in this? The meat is literally melting, but the soup itself... it feels warm when I swallow it, but my internal mana is completely freezing up! In a good way!"
She closed her eyes, letting out a sharp breath. A faint, visible mist escaped her lips, drifting into the warm air of the dining room before vanishing.
Soren watched her reaction closely, keeping his expression neutral despite the sudden leap of anticipation in his chest.
’It’s working!’

His gaze then swept over the rest of the ingredients.

He focused entirely on the workspace before him, letting the lively chatter from the dining room fade into distant background noise.
Cooking with these premium items required extreme precision due to their volatility.
A normal chef might just toss everything into a pot, which would let the elemental essence escape into the air.
To prevent such a waste, Soren had to use his own mana to coat the ingredients, locking the pure frost energy directly inside them during the heating process.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Breakthrough?
paragraphs: ’...Tasty. And...’
Ethea also felt the effects of the meal.
Although she was unable to tell the exact details since she was paralyzed and the only thing she felt was constant pain, she could still tell the meal was actively affecting her, in a good way.
Ethea secretly glanced across the table at Soren.
He was currently smirking at Miss Zoe, leaning back slightly in his chair. "So, are you gonna take those words back?"
Miss Zoe, however, was completely busy with the meal. She kept her head down, purposely ignoring Soren because of embarrassment after being proven wrong so quickly.
However, Ethea doubted it was the only reason.

The sheer intensity of Zoe’s focus suggested something far deeper than mere stubbornness. Seeing how the young woman was discarding her dignity as a woman strengthened Ethea’s certainty in her conclusion.
’This meal is definitely not ordinary.’
Even within the realm of high-tier magical cuisine, this dish was on a whole other level.
’Moreover, it’s specifically prepared for us.’

Ethea’s eyes flickered with a quiet intensity as the realization settled in. The precise balance of the pure frost essence was entirely too specific to be a coincidence. Since Miss Zoe was an ice element user, she likely noticed the profound effects of the dense frost mana immediately, hence the desperate devouring.
’He also asked about Aunt Clara’s affinity yesterday to make sure.’
Turns out, she had grade 4 water affinity.

This meant she would not be harmed by the intense frost energy. In fact, due to the fluid nature of her grade 4 water affinity, she might even benefit immensely from the high-quality refinement of the broth.
However, the same could not be said for everyone.
An ordinary person or a low-ranking cultivator without proper elemental tolerance or the right affinity would have their internal pathways frozen solid the moment the liquid touched their tongue.

Even a seasoned expert with an opposing element, such as fire, would experience a violent, destructive clash within their core if they dared to eat this meal. It was a double-edged sword, completely lethal to the uninvited, yet meticulously tailored to act as a supreme tonic for the three women sitting at the table.
’Soren... He’s too kind.’
Ethea’s lips curled up subconsciously once again as she stared at the young man, a profound warmth melting her icy exterior.
While she remained lost in her quiet revelation, the silence at the table was suddenly broken by a sharp intake of breath beside her.
As the cold energy began to circulate through Clara’s system, her graceful movements stalled. She slowly set her spoon down, her eyes widening in sheer disbelief as she looked up at Soren.
"Soren..." Clara’s voice was barely above a whisper, carrying a tremor of profound shock. "This... what did you do to this food? I... I feel like I can break through at any moment."

"I’m glad it suits your taste, Aunt Clara," Soren replied, his smirk softening into a relaxed smile as he took another sip from his own bowl. "Drink a bit more and if you feel the bottleneck loosening, don’t hold it back. You can use the training room; I had it already prepared."
Clara nodded quickly, her hand trembling slightly as she picked up her spoon. "Then please excuse me."

She took a few more hurried spoonfuls of the translucent broth and a thick bite of the tender marbled beef, letting the intense, refined energy fill her core to the absolute brim. Standing up from her chair, she paused to offer Soren a deep, grateful bow before turning and heading straight toward the training room.

Meanwhile, Zoe finally finished every single drop of her soup. She set the porcelain bowl down with a sharp click, her face flushed red, though it was hard to tell whether it was from the rapid eating or sheer embarrassment. She let out a long, frosty breath that visibly misted in the air.
"Fine! I take it back!" Zoe huffed, crossing her arms and refusing to look him in the eye. "You’re a monstrously good cook. Happy now?"
Soren chuckled quietly, thoroughly satisfied with the reaction. He leaned back in his chair, swirling the remaining liquid in his bowl. "Feel any difference?"

"...Yes." Zoe nodded, her expression suddenly losing its playful edge and turning a bit solemn. She too was sensing her bottleneck loosening. She looked up at him, her gaze tight with urgency. "Actually, I also want to excuse myself if possible. And can you give me some more just in case?"
Soren didn’t question it. Recognizing the critical timing of a breakthrough manifestation, he gave her a firm nod.
"Of course. Just wait for a moment."
He stood up and quickly headed back into the kitchen to package a fresh portion of the magical soup.
Zoe watched his back for a second, then turned her attention entirely toward the other side of the table. Her gaze shifted onto Ethea, looking a bit hopeful and hesitant.
The energetic, teasing older sister persona was completely gone, replaced by the vulnerability of a young cultivator standing on the precipice of a life-changing advancement.
"...Ethea," Zoe spoke softly, her voice dropping to a near whisper. "Can you tell me what I should do for a successful breakthrough? How did it go for you? After all... you were once an Empress."

Ethea paused, her gaze dropping to the clear broth remaining in her bowl as the title she had long discarded echoed in the quiet room. After a long moment, she lifted her head, her calm eyes locking onto Zoe before she gave a slow, deliberate nod.
"A true breakthrough is not about gathering more power, but about gaining absolute mastery over what you already possess," Ethea said, her voice carrying a steady, timeless weight.
She paused, adjusting her tone to ensure her next words anchored themselves deep in Zoe’s mind.

"Do not let the fear of failure or the rush of power break your focus; instead, clear your mind of all external expectations, maintain an unshakeable will against the pressure, and wait for the exact moment your core yields to your command."

chapters.title: Chapter 117: A Vague Truth
paragraphs: Zoe fell silent for a moment, her gaze dropping to the table as she turned the words over in her mind. Her brow furrowed slightly, her lips moving silently as she repeated the core of the advice to herself.
"...Mastery over what I possess... Wait for the right moment..."
A few moments later, the lingering anxiety completely vanished from her expression. She turned back to Ethea, meeting the former Empress’s calm gaze, and gave a deep, respectful nod of gratitude.
"Thank you. I really appreciate it."
Ethea silently accepted the gesture.
Right then, Soren returned from the kitchen carrying a neatly wrapped box.
"Here," he said, handing it to her. "I hope it will be enough."
"Thank you," Zoe said earnestly as she stood up. After taking the container, she turned toward the exit. "I will be taking my leave, then."

However, after taking a few hasty steps, her movements suddenly stalled. She stopped in her tracks, pausing for a brief second before turning back toward the table to lock her eyes directly onto Ethea.
"Think about what I said," she murmured mysteriously, a subtle glint flashing across her eyes.
Ethea stiffened but managed to reply quickly. "...I will."
Satisfied with the response, Zoe turned away and headed out. Soren followed to see her off, walking beside her all the way until they stepped outside.
As they walked, Soren finally broke the silence, curiosity getting the better of him. "So, what exactly did the two of you talk about while I was cooking?"
Zoe stopped in the hallway, turning to face him with a playful smile. "It’s women’s secret talk. A gentleman shouldn’t pry into it."
"Oh, okay then," Soren chuckled, choosing not to push the matter any further. He still made sure to give her an encouraging nod, though. "I wish you success."
"Thanks. I won’t disappoint," Zoe said, giving a confident little wave before heading off.

Soren watched her figure disappear as she entered the lift before stepping back inside. Closing the door and his eyes, he focused inward on his own core. A heavy, vibrant warmth was pulsing directly against the boundaries of his core.
He too was incredibly close to a breakthrough.
The residual energy from preparing the dish, combined with the few bites he had taken himself, was already pushing his cultivation forward at an alarming rate.
’It seems like the effects are more potent than I anticipated.’
Opening his eyes, he exhaled a long breath to stabilize the sudden surge. There was still business to attend to before he could focus entirely on his own cultivation.
’Let’s check up on Aunt Clara first.’

Approaching the training room, he extended his perception toward the reinforced door. He easily sensed Clara sitting cross-legged in the center of the chamber, already initiating her breakthrough. The water mana around her flowed with smooth, rhythmic precision, showing absolutely no signs of instability.
Sensing nothing wrong, he turned back to the dining area and sat down beside Ethea.
"How was it?" he asked, breaking the quiet as he glanced at her mostly uneaten bowl. "Was the taste good?"
Ethea looked up, her calm eyes meeting his. "Yes, it is really delicious. Thank you for your hard work."
"Hmm, as long as you’re satisfied, it’s good," Soren replied with a faint smile.
Ethea hesitated for a fraction of a second, her fingers twitching. "...Soren, can I ask you something?"
"Sure, go ahead."
"...Where did you learn to cook these dishes?"
"..." Soren fell silent at the unexpected question.
On second thought, he should have expected it from someone with Ethea’s analytical personality.
’...Should I say I found it on the Golden Gate again?’
If he made an excuse and ’revealed’ that he found even more treasures, it would sound plausible. However, he didn’t want to lie to her. Not again.
Noticing his hesitation, Ethea softly added, "You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to.
"Well... It’s not that I don’t want to," Soren said, scratching the back of his neck with a wry smile. "It’s just a bit difficult to explain. Let’s just say... it’s related to my ability."
"...I see," Ethea muttered, offering a small, understanding nod. A faint trace of satisfaction appeared in her eyes, appreciating the fact that he had done his best to give her an honest answer.
Soren leaned back slightly, shifting the momentum of the conversation. "...Can I ask you something too?"
"Go ahead."
"I think I am gonna break through as well, so... got any advice?"
Ethea paused, her hand freezing completely.
’So fast?’
It had only been just over a month since he awakened, yet he is already about to break through to the third circle?
’It must be related to the Golden Gate...’ She guessed after a quick mental analysis. ’Ryan had also broken through to the 2nd Circle peak during the ordeal after all.’
’Then...’
She took a deep breath and turned her head to stare directly at him, her usual indifferent, piercing expression returning to her face.
"You... you practice the Glacial Emperor Scripture, right?"

"...Yes," Soren replied after a brief pause, now unsurprised by her question. He knew better than to play dumb with a former Empress who likely knew the technique inside out. "And, if you are worried, I didn’t get it from your father or any of your family members. I didn’t steal it or obtain it through underhanded means either, so you can rest assured. But... I can’t tell you how I got it for a similar reason to earlier."
He kept his expression neutral, keeping his deeper thoughts to himself.
’In fact, I haven’t accepted a single thing from them. Well, except those cards.’

Soren had purposefully stashed away both the business and credit cards her father had given him during that sudden visit. He had no intention of spending a single credit from it, even if his own accounts ran completely dry. He refused to owe that family anything, and more importantly, he simply didn’t trust them after the cold, calculating way they had abandoned Ethea.

Moreover, they hadn’t visited her once after dropping her off, nor had they sent a single message to check on her condition. The timing of that visit and the sheer amount of money left behind felt entirely too transactional, almost like hush money or a severance package to wipe their hands clean of a crippled daughter.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Breakthrough! [2]
paragraphs: Something about that man’s entire demeanor during their brief encounter left a lingering, unsettling taste in Soren’s mouth. The more he reflected on that interaction, the more a quiet suspicion began to take root in his mind.
Although he had looked like a regretful, loving parent on the surface, it was highly probable that the entire display was nothing more than an act.
Her father was definitely keeping secrets.
’I’m sure of it.’
Ethea broke the silence, her gaze softening slightly as she looked at him.
"Mmm. I believe you. And... thank you... for telling me all of this," she said softly.
Soren let out a small, relieved breath and nodded, glad to move past the topic. "So, back to my question. Since I do practice it... got any advice?"
Ethea paused for a moment, her usual indifferent, analytical expression returning as she took a deep breath to focus on the technicalities of the cultivation technique.

"As you might have already noticed, the Glacial Emperor Scripture is fundamentally different from standard cultivation techniques," she explained, her voice naturally adopting a calm, instructive tone.

"For conventional cultivators, reaching the Third Circle requires opening all the hidden pathways in the body to let mana circulate freely to the surface. This allows them to manifest a thin, protective layer of mana around their skin that can be toggled on and off at will once mastered. In our world, that surface layer itself is commonly considered the third layer, marking someone as a true Third Circle cultivator."

Soren listened intently, his focus sharpening. "Right. From what I’ve researched, conventional methods rely on a highly controlled, synchronized resonance. They accelerate the two layers of the core to a specific frequency, creating an internal pressure that expands the pathways outward until the mana naturally bleeds through to the skin’s surface."
He shifted slightly, looking directly at her.

"But the scripture explicitly warns against that expansion. If I try to force the cold outward, it will just freeze the unawakened pathways solid and fracture my internal network. The scripture says I need to lock both existing layers into absolute stillness instead, but it’s incredibly vague on the actual transition. Since you’ve mastered this exact progression, what’s the trick to making it work?"
Ethea observed him for a quiet moment, a faint glimmer of approval passing through her eyes before her expression smoothed out.

"The trick is understanding that your reward is twice what a conventional cultivator achieves," Ethea said softly. "They only gain the surface layer. But because you drive your core into absolute stillness, the resulting internal implosion will violently snap open every single pathway at once, flooding your skin. But it doesn’t stop there."
Soren nodded, indicating he was focusing.

"The sheer volume of mana pulled back from that sudden expansion will condense right at the center of your chest. It will forge a third internal layer around your core. While ordinary cultivators only have a fragile skin film, you will have a dual boundary. A permanent armor on your skin, and an impenetrable shield guarding your core inside."
Soren’s eyebrows raised slightly. "A dual boundary. That sounds incredibly powerful, but holding that much pressure must be a nightmare."

"It is," Ethea agreed completely. "And that is where the danger lies. When the stillness peaks and the pathways snap open, the mana will want to scatter chaotically between your skin and your chest. To stabilize it, you must not panic when your body goes completely numb. You have to use your intent to anchor the mana to both your heartbeat and your skin simultaneously. If you lose focus for even a second during that dual synchronization, the backflow will destroy your pathways permanently."
Soren nodded slowly, gulping inwardly at the sheer seriousness of the process.

Cultivation always promised incredible power, but the risks paired with it were equally terrifying. One wrong move, one moment of panicked hesitation, and he would permanently ruin his future before it even truly began.
Ethea seemed to read the tension in his shoulders. Her eyes softened slightly, and she spoke in a reassuring tone.

"You do not have to worry too much, Soren. Your affinity is exceptionally high, and your control and talent have already proven themselves during your previous breakthrough. As long as you remain calm and avoid major mistakes, you are more than capable of handling it."
Hearing her objective assessment did wonders to ease the heavy weight in his chest. "Thanks for the help, Ethea. I really appreciate it."
"Don’t mention it." The corners of her lips curved upward into a rare smile. "This is the least I can do as your wife."
A subtle warmth bloomed in Soren’s chest at her words.
’My wife, huh...’
A comfortable sweetness settled into the room, making him forget about the dangers of the breakthrough for a brief moment.

Just then, a sudden, powerful wave of mana rippled through the entire house, enveloping them both in a gentle, warm pressure. The ambient energy vibrated with a rhythmic, steady pulse that signaled a perfect stabilization of power from the adjacent room.
The two of them exchanged a knowing look and smiled at each other simultaneously.
’Auntie had broken through successfully.’
Even their thoughts seemed to align perfectly in that quiet moment of shared relief.

Soren let out a quiet chuckle, the sudden burst of celebratory energy perfectly cutting through the lingering seriousness in the atmosphere. He shifted his attention back to the table, picking up the bowl of broth that had cooled slightly during their conversation.
"Well, let’s finish this before she comes out to celebrate," Soren said, offering the spoon back to Ethea.

Ethea did not refuse. For the next few minutes, a peaceful silence returned to the room, broken only by the soft clink of the spoon. Soren carefully fed her the remaining warm broth, occasionally taking a sip from his own bowl until both were completely empty.
Just as Soren was setting the bowls down, the door to the adjacent room clicked open.

Clara stepped out into the hallway, a vibrant, visible glow surrounding her. The physical toll of her previous fatigue seemed completely erased. Her skin possessed a flawless, radiant clarity, and the faint lines of stress around her eyes had completely vanished, replaced by an unmistakable vitality.
"Whoa!" Soren’s eyes widened slightly as he took in her appearance. "You look a lot younger, Auntie! Congratulations on your breakthrough."
Ethea looked toward the doorway as well, a gentle warmth reflecting in her gaze. "Congratulations, Aunt Clara."

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Breakthrough! [3]
paragraphs: Clara’s eyes lit up at their words, a brilliant spark of genuine joy lighting her face. Her radiant expression quickly gave way to deep, heartfelt solemnity as she stepped closer and bowed deeply at the waist toward the young couple.

"Thank you... Thank you so much for your selflessness," Clara said, her voice trembling slightly with emotion. "Without your support, Soren... I wouldn’t have been able to overcome this wall. I am entirely in your debt."
Soren accepted her gratitude with a calm nod, recognizing that letting her express her thanks was the best way to ease her mind. He stood up from his seat, stacking the empty bowls neatly.

"You earned this breakthrough, Auntie, so please don’t overthink it," Soren said warmly. "You can continue the dinner. As for me, I also need to go and absorb the insights from earlier while my mind is fresh."
"Yes, yes, go ahead!" Clara replied hurriedly, quickly stepping to the side to clear the path for him.

Nodding, Soren left the two alone and entered the training room, sitting cross-legged on the mat. The two existing circles inside his chest rotated with a familiar, rhythmic hum, glowing with a deep, frosty light.
’Time to begin.’
With a sharp pull of his intent, he clamped down on his core.

The reaction was instantaneous and agonizing. Forcing those spinning layers to a sudden halt felt like trying to stop a speeding flywheel with his bare hands. A jagged shockwave of absolute cold rippled out from his chest, dropping his internal temperature as a crushing pressure settled over his heart.

He pushed his will harder against the resisting mana, sending lines of burning, icy pain radiating outward. His teeth chattered violently, frost instantly coating his lips. The two layers wobbled under the immense restraint, fighting to resume their natural spin.
’Hold still...’
Soren poured everything he had into the suppression, freezing the rotation until it snapped into a dead, absolute standstill.

The moment the core stopped, the space between the two frozen layers collapsed inward, creating a massive, terrifying vacuum at his center. That sudden internal void acted like a black hole, violently pulling from every corner of his anatomy. The extreme negative pressure dragged the dormant air and stagnant energy right out of his closed meridians.
CRACK...
CRACK...
Under the immense suction of the vacuum, every single hidden pathway throughout his body violently snapped open at once.

The sudden release of pressure caused the compressed mana to rebound, bursting out of his core like a tidal wave. It flooded the newly opened channels and rushed toward the surface of his skin. Thousands of frozen needles drove through his flesh, turning his entire body completely numb. He couldn’t feel his hands, his legs, or even the ground beneath him.
’Now!’

Fighting the blinding agony and the terrifying loss of sensation, Soren split his focus. He grabbed the runaway mana at the surface of his skin to anchor it into a perimeter, while simultaneously pulling the massive backflow inward to fill the vacuum of his chest.

The pressure inside him doubled. His heart hammered wildly against the frozen constraints as he forced the dual synchronization to hold. It felt as if his chest would rupture from the sheer density of the trapped energy.
Then, the chaotic forces reached their peak and locked into place.

The mana on his skin snapped into a perfect boundary just beneath the surface. At the exact same microsecond, the internal backflow condensed around his core, forging a solid, physical third internal ring.
The overwhelming pressure vanished in an instant.
Soren’s muscles gave out entirely, and he collapsed backward onto the mat.
"Huff... Huff..."
He lay there staring blankly at the ceiling, breathing in ragged gasps.
He was completely drenched, his clothes soaked through with a mixture of icy sweat and the dark, foul impurities violently purged from his pathways.
A sharp, pungent odor quickly filled the room, the foul smell of impurities making Soren grimace.
His nose wrinkled in immediate disgust, but with his muscles entirely drained and trembling from the breakthrough, he could do nothing but lie there and endure it for a few long minutes.

Once a fraction of strength returned to his limbs, he forced himself up. Gritting his teeth against the lingering aches, he dragged his heavy body across the floor and slipped into the attached bathroom inside the training room.

He spent nearly half an hour under the water, scrubbing away the dark residue and the stubborn stench until his skin was entirely clean. Stepping out of the shower, he wiped the condensation off the mirror to check his reflection.
"Whoa..."
An involuntary whisper of admiration escaped his lips.
The physical transformation was undeniable.
The impurities had been thoroughly washed away, leaving his skin noticeably paler and smoother, almost carrying a faint, ethereal luster characteristic of high-tier Awakened.

His frame had leaned out perfectly; his muscles were tightly defined without being overly bulky, and his abdomen had sharpened into an almost flawless, sculpted six-pack. He looked completely rejuvenated, possessing a sleek kind of athleticism.
Soren stared for a moment longer, letting out a quiet sigh of appreciation for the perks of the breakthrough.
’Alright, that is enough.’
Shaking off the daze, he quickly dressed in a fresh set of clothes and stepped back out into the training room.

The moment he opened the bathroom door, a soft hum vibrated through the walls. The room’s automated ventilation and purification arrays had already finished running. The dark residue on the mat had been neutralized, and the air was completely crisp, carrying a faint, clean scent instead of the foul odor from before.
’This is what you call a luxurious apartment~.’
Satisfied, Soren left the training room and walked back into the main living area.

The dining table had already been completely cleared of the dinner bowls. Clara and Ethea were sitting together, enjoying some light snacks while occasionally glancing toward the hallway. The moment Soren stepped into the light, both of their eyes snapped to him.
Soren rubbed the back of his neck, offering an apologetic smile. "Sorry, I made you wait too long."
Clara and Ethea both shook their heads immediately.
"No, not at all," Clara said, waving her hand dismissively with a bright smile. "We were just enjoying some tea. Besides, you look completely refreshed."
"You took less time than expected," Ethea added, her eyes narrowing slightly as she swept her gaze over his altered appearance, noting the subtle shift in his presence.
"Right! Congratulations!" Clara said warmly. "Whatever insights you were processing, it looks like your session was incredibly successful."

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Breakthrough Returns
paragraphs: Clara excused herself shortly after, claiming she needed to rest and let her newly stabilized core settle.
Soren then shared the details of his breakthrough process with Ethea, who congratulated him on the success.
They wound down by watching a single episode of a TV show before heading to the bedroom. Soren tucked her into bed, sat down on his mattress, and opened his status.
[PERSONAL INFORMATION]
Name: Soren Everly
Age: 22
Circle Rank: Third Circle (Early Stage)
Hunter Rank: E
[CORE STATUS]
Mana Capacity: 57,860 / 150,000
Core Stability: Optimal
Pathway Integrity: Excellent
Affinity: Ice (Grade 7 — S Rank) | Wind (Grade 5 — B Rank)
’...Amazing.’
Soren mumbled inwardly, staring at the translucent blue window.

His mana capacity had tripled this time, reaching a staggering 150,000. It was an absurd number, especially when he recalled the standard scale for conventional cultivators. A typical Second Circle cultivator usually possessed around 20,000 to 25,000 mana, yet he had held 50,000. Now, while the average Third Circle cultivator peaked at about 50,000, his foundation boasted triple that amount.

The gap between him and his peers was widening into a chasm, or more like he was chasing them at an alarming rate. To put it into perspective, a genuinely talented person like Sister Zoe had around 500,000 mana at the peak of the Fifth Circle. If he continued at this current rhythm, his capacity would easily eclipse hers by the time he reached that level.
Yet, as intoxicating as the numbers were, Soren forced himself to calm down, shaking away the rising pride.
The world was vast, and there were probably more hidden geniuses out there than he knew. His own wife, Ethea, must have been a once-in-a-generation monster before her accident.
’I wonder how much her capacity was back then?’ he wondered briefly, before shaking the thought away.

Regardless of others, this breakthrough meant he was officially qualified to enter Third Circle gates. However, he quickly decided to put that plan on hold. Entering those gates meant taking a hunter promotion exam. He had only just taken his last exam not long ago; pushing for another rank advancement so quickly would undoubtedly raise suspicion and draw unwanted attention to himself.
Come to think of it, ’they’ hadn’t taken any action since the first exam.
Could it be that they were just watching him for now, with no immediate intention of intervening? Because he had already met with an accident. Or... was his recent suspicion holding some truth to it?
’...I will have to talk with Ethea about it soon,’ he sighed, casting a brief glance toward the quiet bed where she lay resting.
Turning his attention back to the floating interface, Soren’s eyes landed on a familiar, glowing notification icon blinking in the upper corner.
’Good, it worked.’
A satisfied smile played on his lips. He opened the notification window, read the info, and tapped ’Yes’ without hesitation.
Instantly, a cascade of investment messages flooded his vision.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Clara]
[Analyzing investment...]

[Investment: You treated the target not as a mere employee, but as close family, welcoming her to your table to share a rare, highly valuable meal you personally prepared. By providing this resource and supporting her through the breakthrough, you directly enabled her to overcome a long-standing wall.]
[Analyzing target response...]

[As a result of your actions, the target successfully broke through her bottleneck, restoring her faded vitality and extending her lifespan by ten years. The breakthrough has profoundly elevated her mana purity. Furthermore, experiencing your respect and hospitality, the target’s perspective has shifted; she has dropped her strict professional distance and begun to genuinely view and treat you and your wife like close family.]
[Evaluating investment...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: High]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Returns granted:]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
[1. Permanent Mana Capacity Expansion (+10,000)]
[2. Rare Recipe: Abyssal Tide Stew — A water-element oriented culinary blueprint designed to accelerate pathway conditioning and optimize mana circulation for water or ice affinity users.]
[3. Rare Recipe: Glacial Dew Mochi — A specialized dessert blueprint that temporarily stabilizes core fluctuations and provides a mild boost to mental clarity.]
[4. Life Force Resonance (C-Rank) — Passively enhances the user’s natural vitality and extends physical endurance.]
[5. Perceptive Eye (D-Rank) — Grants the ability to subtly sense the emotional baseline and sincerity of those nearby.]
[Integration initiated...]
The integration initiated immediately, a warm wave of energy reshaping his core, evolving his vision, and etching the intricate culinary knowledge straight into his mind.
[Integration complete!]

As the message flashed and faded, Soren took a deep breath, letting it out slowly. Looking over the listed returns, the haul was much better than he had anticipated, likely a combined result of his Amplification passive and the sheer quality of the investment itself.

He glanced back at his core status. Not only had his maximum limit risen, but his current mana pool had also instantly filled by an additional 10,000 points. A satisfied hum escaped his lips; he hadn’t expected the system to grant direct capacity expansions like this. But recalling how he got his Grade 7 Ice affinity, it made sense.

And the two new abilities were a welcome addition to his arsenal, providing utility he sorely lacked. As for the rare recipes, reading the detailed cooking instructions flashing in his mind gave him another amusing urge to abandon hunting entirely and just become a full-time chef. At the very least, it would make for a highly profitable side job.
The potential of these culinary blueprints made him lean back, his mind naturally wandering to his other ongoing commitments.
If the returns from Aunt Clara were this substantial, what kind of rewards would he get from his investment in Sister Zoe?

Though the thought filled him with genuine anticipation, Soren shook his head to clear it. Her safety and success came first above all else. Regardless of the investment returns, he truly wanted her to overcome her trials and succeed.
’Come to think of it, it usually takes anywhere from a week to several months to successfully break through to the Sixth Circle.’
Given the immense complexity of that threshold, Zoe would likely remain in seclusion for a while, meaning he would have to wait patiently for the final results of that investment.
’Until then, I just need to keep building my own strength step by step.’

Turning his attention back to the floating interface, Soren’s eyes landed on a familiar, glowing notification icon blinking in the upper corner.
’Good, it worked.’
A satisfied smile played on his lips.
He opened the notification window, read the info, and tapped ’Yes’ without hesitation.
Instantly, a cascade of investment messages flooded his vision.
[Investment detected.]
[Target: Clara]
[Analyzing investment...]
[Investment: You treated the target not as a mere employee, but as close family, welcoming her to your table to share a rare, highly valuable meal you personally prepared.
By providing this resource and supporting her through the breakthrough, you directly enabled her to overcome a long-standing wall.]
[Analyzing target response...]
[As a result of your actions, the target successfully broke through her bottleneck, restoring her faded vitality and extending her lifespan by ten years.
The breakthrough has profoundly elevated her mana purity.

Furthermore, experiencing your respect and hospitality, the target’s perspective has shifted; she has dropped her strict professional distance and begun to genuinely view and treat you and your wife like close family.]
[Evaluating investment...]
[Evaluation complete.]
[Investment Grade: High]
[Calculating returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Returns granted:]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) — Baseline bonus applied.
Reward tier scaling upgraded.]
[Returns granted:]
Permanent Mana Capacity Expansion (+10,000)]
Rare Recipe: Abyssal Tide Stew — A water-element oriented culinary blueprint designed to accelerate pathway conditioning and optimize mana circulation for water or ice affinity users.]
Rare Recipe: Glacial Dew Mochi — A specialized dessert blueprint that temporarily stabilizes core fluctuations and provides a mild boost to mental clarity.]
Life Force Resonance (C-Rank) — Passively enhances the user’s natural vitality and extends physical endurance.]
Perceptive Eye (D-Rank) — Grants the ability to subtly sense the emotional baseline and sincerity of those nearby.]
[Integration initiated...]
The integration initiated immediately, a warm wave of energy reshaping his core, evolving his vision, and etching the intricate culinary knowledge straight into his mind.
[Integration complete!]
As the message flashed and faded, Soren took a deep breath, letting it out slowly.
Looking over the listed returns, the haul was much better than he had anticipated, likely a combined result of his Amplification passive and the sheer quality of the investment itself.
He glanced back at his core status.
Not only had his maximum limit risen, but his current mana pool had also instantly filled by an additional 10,000 points.
A satisfied hum escaped his lips; he hadn’t expected the system to grant direct capacity expansions like this.
But recalling how he got his Grade 7 Ice affinity, it made sense.
And the two new abilities were a welcome addition to his arsenal, providing utility he sorely lacked.
As for the rare recipes, reading the detailed cooking instructions flashing in his mind gave him another amusing urge to abandon hunting entirely and just become a full-time chef.
At the very least, it would make for a highly profitable side job.
The potential of these culinary blueprints made him lean back, his mind naturally wandering to his other ongoing commitments.
If the returns from Aunt Clara were this substantial, what kind of rewards would he get from his investment in Sister Zoe?
Though the thought filled him with genuine anticipation, Soren shook his head to clear it.
Her safety and success came first above all else.
Regardless of the investment returns, he truly wanted her to overcome her trials and succeed.
’Come to think of it, it usually takes anywhere from a week to several months to successfully break through to the Sixth Circle.’
Given the immense complexity of that threshold, Zoe would likely remain in seclusion for a while, meaning he would have to wait patiently for the final results of that investment.
’Until then, I just need to keep building my own strength step by step.’

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Visiting The Bureau [1]
paragraphs: Two days later, Soren found himself back at the awakening bureau.

He had already stabilized his cultivation and even gone on three raids, but today his focus was entirely logistical. The bureau had finally completed its initial research on the monolith, and he was here to negotiate the official ownership and rights regarding the anomaly.

Thankfully, he didn’t have to wait in the main lobby for long. Almost as soon as he stepped through the entrance, he was welcomed by Administrator Veyra herself. Her presence alone drew a few curious glances from nearby hunters and staff, signaling the importance of the meeting and her status.

"Good to see you, Soren," Veyra said, offering a professional nod before gesturing toward the secure elevators. "The research team wrapped up their primary analysis ahead of schedule. We’re heading upstairs now to meet with the head of the Kalmira Awakened Bureau to discuss the details."
Soren nodded, falling into step beside her as they moved through the polished corridors toward the secure elevator bank.

As they walked, Veyra looked over at him, her expression a mix of professional curiosity and genuine interest. "How has your experience with the bureau membership been so far? Have you been utilizing the benefits fully?"

"It’s been great," Soren replied with an appreciative nod. "Especially the internal shop. The prices for cultivation materials and gear are significantly lower than anything you can find out on the open hunter market."

Veyra smiled, a look of quiet professional pride crossing her features. "Good to hear. We strive to provide our hunters with the best possible environment to grow and sustain themselves. After all, your safety directly translates to the city’s stability."

She paused briefly as they reached the elevator, pressing the button for the top executive floors. Before the doors slid open, she glanced back at him. "Have you given any thoughts to upgrading your membership tier?"
Soren shook his head smoothly, offering a polite but firm response. "No, I haven’t really had the time lately, and my current tier is pretty good for my needs right now."

"Fair enough," Veyra said, gesturing for him to step into the elevator ahead of her. "But let me know if you change your mind. The higher tiers also unlock direct access to more gates and priority access to rare resources. It’s an option always open to someone of your caliber."
Soren nodded. "I will keep that in mind."

As the elevator began its smooth ascent, the professional atmosphere inside the cabin shifted. Veyra hesitated briefly, looking away for a fraction of a second before facing him with a slight furrow in her brow.

"Mr. Soren... I wanted to apologize for the recent incident," she said, her tone softening into genuine regret. "I couldn’t step in to help you or visit you while the investigation was ongoing. I wanted to mobilize our branch’s legal team right away, but the higher-ups explicitly told me that everything was under control and ordered me not to intervene.

Soren shook his head smoothly, offering her a reassuring expression. "No, you don’t have to apologize for that. Thank you for worrying about my situation regardless. Thankfully, it all got resolved without any further incident."
"That is true," Veyra agreed, letting out a small, weary sigh. "But it is still a shame. We lost a few very promising hunter candidates all because of one culprit’s actions."

Soren chose to remain silent, offering no verbal comment on her observation. He knew exactly who she was talking about. She was undoubtedly referring to the remaining members of Team 14, who had received severe disciplinary punishments for assisting Garin Vale in his malicious scheme. The academy had expelled them entirely, and the bureau had slapped them with a three-year ban from all hunter activities, including entering any licensed gates. On top of that, they were currently serving three months in a juvenile correctional facility to rehabilitate their psychological baselines.

This might have looked lenient on the surface, but the reality was different. They had received a lesser punishment primarily because they had also become victims of Garin’s extreme actions during the final moments; they had turned themselves in, fully cooperated with the investigation, and acted as key witnesses to expose the truth.

If they could genuinely endure this hardship, a consequence entirely born from their own poor choices, and truly reflect on their actions, they might actually have a chance to reform. With the right guidance during their time in the correctional facility, they could still turn their lives around and eventually become good hunters and decent people.
However, his internal reflections were abruptly disrupted by a soft chime. The elevator ground to a smooth halt, and the heavy doors slid open to reveal a carpeted, high-security executive hallway.
"Follow me," Veyra said, stepping out into the corridor.

Soren stepped out behind her, his shoes sinking slightly into the plush, sound-dampening carpet. The corridor was quiet, lined with dark wood paneling and minimalist mana-lighting that gave the entire floor an air of heavy authority.
Veyra led him to a set of double frosted-glass doors at the very end of the hall.

Stepping inside, Soren found himself in a spacious, sunlit office with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the Kalmira skyline. Behind a massive mahogany desk sat a middle-aged man, meticulously reviewing a floating holographic document. He possessed sharp, neat white hair and a well-groomed white beard that added a striking sense of discipline to his strong jawline.
As the man looked up, Soren felt a sudden, inexplicable prickle of familiarity.
There was something in the sharp structure of the man’s eyes and the subtle, commanding tilt of his brow that looked strangely reminiscent of someone he knew.
Curious, Soren discreetly activated Investor’s Insight.
A subtle, translucent ripple passed over his vision, and a detailed status screen materialized, instantly stiffening Soren’s posture in surprise.
Name: Craig Marron
Status: Healthy
Age: 43
Rank: 6th Circle (Mid Stage)
Current Mana Level: Very High (1,735,878)
Ability: Sovereign Aura
Mental State: Analytical, Highly Curious
Investment Value: High
Potential: 7th Circle (Estimated)
’He’s her relative?!’

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Visiting The Bureau [2]
paragraphs: The middle-aged man closed the floating holographic document with a brief wave of his hand and stood up from behind the massive mahogany desk. Despite his high rank, he didn’t project an overbearing pressure; his movements were smooth, deliberate, and perfectly composed.
Coming around the desk, he extended a hand toward the young hunter, a polite, welcoming smile touching his lips. "Hunter Soren, it is a pleasure to meet you."
Soren recovered from his internal surprise within a fraction of a second, his expression remaining perfectly calm and natural. He reached out, firmly shaking the man’s hand.
"No, the pleasure is all mine, Mr..." Soren let his voice trail off slightly, perfectly executing the act of a low-ranking hunter meeting a high-level bureau official for the first time.
"Craig. Craig Marron," the man supplied smoothly, his sharp eyes evaluating Soren with a look of quiet interest.
"Right, Mr. Craig." Soren nodded in appreciation.

"Please, have a seat," Craig said, gesturing toward the comfortable leather armchairs positioned in front of his desk. He turned his attention toward the administrator. "Administrator Veyra, would you mind telling the secretary to bring us some coffee or tea?"
"Of course, Director," Veyra replied with a professional nod, turning back toward the double doors to convey the request.
While she stepped out of the office for a brief moment, an easy silence settled between the two men. Craig walked back over to his side of the desk, leaning against the edge in a relaxed posture.

"You’ve been making quite a name for yourself recently, Hunter Soren," Craig remarked conversationally, his tone casual yet attentive. "An E-rank solo hunter managing to handle complex situations efficiently is a rare sight in Kalmira."
"I simply do my best to complete my assignments safely, Mr. Craig," Soren replied smoothly, keeping his posture relaxed. "Meticulous preparation usually saves a lot of trouble."
Craig let out a soft chuckle. "A wise philosophy. Too many young hunters rely entirely on brute strength and realize their mistake far too late."

The door clicked open again, and Veyra returned, sliding effortlessly back into her position beside the desk. The brief moment of casual small talk concluded instantly, shifting back into a focused, professional atmosphere.

"Now, down to business," Craig said, straightening up and looking directly at Soren. "I am sure you have already been notified, but our research team finished analyzing the monolith ahead of schedule. We have successfully determined its primary effects and exact grade. The good news is that the anomaly is completely stable and poses absolutely no threat to the city or people. However, because of its unique nature, I would still like to negotiate its official ownership and rights with you.
Soren nodded slowly. "What exactly is it that you want to discuss regarding the ownership?"

"Well, first let me explain what we discovered about its identity and capabilities," Craig explained, folding his arms. "Once we establish that, we can move on to the specific proposal we prepared for you."
"I am ready to listen," Soren replied, keeping his expression neutral.
"Good. Administrator Veyra, show him the documents."
Veyra nodded, pulling out a sleek, high-grade data tablet and handing it over to Soren.
Soren took the device and tapped the screen, scrolling through the comprehensive breakdown.
As he read the bureau’s analytical findings, he noted how closely they aligned with what his Investor’s Insight had originally revealed to him.

The report classified the monolith as a unique utility artifact. Its primary function is to draw raw, unfiltered energy directly from the surrounding atmosphere and compress it into a highly refined state. By doing so, it generates a localized high-density mana zone, effectively tripling the cultivation speed of anyone training within its active radius. The report also listed a few minor secondary effects, such as stabilizing ambient mana fluctuations and gently cleansing impurities from the immediate air supply.
After reviewing the full technical readout, Soren powered down the screen, handed the tablet back to Veyra, and turned his attention back to the director.
"Oh? You don’t seem particularly surprised by the findings," Craig observed, a small, knowing smile playing on his lips as he noticed the young hunter’s lack of a dramatic reaction.

Soren, already anticipating the question, gave a casual shrug. "Well, I already had my doubts and theories about its nature after being in close contact with it. Seeing your report simply confirmed those initial suspicions, though I actually managed to learn a few more technical details than I originally anticipated. Your research team truly did an exceptional job.
"Yeah, they did," Craig said, a genuine smile breaking through his professional demeanor. "Those fools actually managed to do something useful for once."
He walked back around his desk and took his seat, leaning forward slightly as the mood in the room grew serious. "Anyway, should we get to the main topic now?"
"Mm," Soren nodded, settling back into his chair.

"Good. Then here is our offer," Craig began, tapping a finger on the desk to emphasize his words. "The bureau would like to buy the full ownership of the monolith from you. In exchange, we will provide you with—"
"No," Soren interrupted decisively, his voice cutting through the director’s sentence with absolute finality. "I won’t sell it."
Craig paused, his extended hand freezing mid-air. The office went incredibly quiet for a moment.
"Well..." Craig breathed out, a look of unexpected amusement flashing across his sharp features as he lowered his hand. "That was quite a blunt rejection."
"I apologize for that, Mr. Craig," Soren said, maintaining his polite composure despite the decisive refusal.
Craig let out a low chuckle, leaning back in his leather chair. "You certainly don’t look like you do, Hunter Soren."

Soren chose to remain silent, offering no verbal defense as a slight wave of inward embarrassment washed over him. He knew he had broken professional etiquette, but protecting the monolith was a boundary he couldn’t afford to compromise on.

"Well, we expected this outcome anyway," Craig continued smoothly, completely unbothered by the rejection. "I simply asked in case you would happen to agree and save us a bit of paperwork. Since that is out of the question, let me give you our real offer."
